English: IEBC Electoral Code Committee Finds Nakuru Town East MP Guilty of Code of Conduct Breach14th Jul 2026. The IEBC Electoral Code of Conduct Enforcement Committee, chaired by Commissioner Dr. Alutalala Mukhwana, has found the Member of the National Assembly for Nakuru Town East, Hon. David Gikaria, guilty of breaching the Electoral Code of Conduct. The Committee imposed several sanctions, including directing the legislator to issue a public apology and formally retract the offending remarks. He was also warned against committing similar violations in future, with the Committee cautioning that any subsequent breaches will attract more severe penalties, including the possibility of being barred from participating in elective politics. Additionally, Hon. Gikaria has been ordered to pay a fine of KSh 2.5 million within 48 hours. The Committee has also referred the matter to the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions (ODPP) for investigation into possible offences under the Election Offences Act. #16thJulyByElection #YourVoteYourVoice #TalkWithIEBC #StopFakeNews

English: IEBC Presents Electoral Reforms and 2027 General Election Preparedness to Senate Committee12th Jun 2026. The Commission today appeared before the Senate Standing Committee on Justice, Legal Affairs and Human Rights (JLAHRC), led by Chairperson Senator Hillary K. Sigei, CBS, to present submissions on electoral legal reforms and the Commission's preparedness for the 2027 General Election. The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) was led by Deputy Commission Secretary – Operations, Ruth Kulundu, who represented the Ag. Commission Secretary/CEO, Moses Sunkuli, OGW. During the session, the Commission outlined a series of strategic, operational, institutional and legal interventions aimed at ensuring timely and effective preparation for the upcoming General Election. Kulundu informed the Committee that the Commission's Strategic Plan 2024–2029 and Election Operations Plan 2025–2027 have been finalised and will be launched soon. The two strategic documents provide a comprehensive framework for delivering the IEBC’s constitutional mandate and identify key interventions aimed at strengthening participation, inclusion, citizen engagement, promoting equitable representation and enhancing institutional resilience. The Election Operations Plan serves as the primary roadmap for planning, coordinating and implementing electoral activities in the lead-up to the 2027 General Election. The Commission reaffirmed its commitment to delivering a credible, transparent, inclusive and efficient electoral process, and emphasized that preparations for the 2027 General Election remain firmly on course. #16thJulyByelection #KuraYakoSautiYako #IEBCStrategicPlan #IEBCEOP

English: IEBC Holds Planning Meeting Ahead of Ol-Kalou Parliamentary By-Election19th May 2026. The Commission today held a planning meeting ahead of the Ol-Kalou Constituency parliamentary by-election scheduled for 16th July 2026. The meeting brought together election officials to review preparedness and align operational plans for the upcoming exercise. Speaking during the meeting, Commissioner Ann Nderitu, CBS officially opened the session and emphasized areas critical to the successful conduct of the by-election. These included data protection, photography within the polling booth, access control at polling centres, and the expected conduct of election officials throughout the electoral process. The planning meeting provided a platform for officials to share lessons learned from previous elections, identify emerging issues requiring intervention, and develop appropriate mitigation measures. Participants also reviewed key by-election activities, timelines, budgets, operational procedures, and expectations as part of the Commission’s preparations to deliver a free, fair and credible election. #16thJulyByelection #YourVoteYourFuture #TalkWithIEBC #StopFakeNews

English: IEBC, Ministry of Interior Hold Consultative Meeting Ahead of 2027 General Election15th May 2026. The Commission today, in Nairobi, held a consultative meeting with the Ministry of Interior and National Administration. The engagement focused on strengthening collaboration, particularly in the area of issuance of national identification cards, election security preparedness and conflict management and peacebuilding. While addressing the meeting, the Cabinet Secretary for Interior and National Administration, Kipchumba Murkomen, assured the Commission of the Ministry’s commitment to continuous collaboration and consultation to ensure that the 2027 General Election is credible, peaceful, and reflective of the fundamental principles of good governance. IEBC Chairperson, Erastus Edung Ethekon, thanked the Ministry for its support during the recently concluded Enhanced Continuous Voter Registration drive, as well as the by-elections conducted peacefully on Thursday, May 14. “Today’s engagement is both timely and necessary. Elections are not the responsibility of a single institution. Successful elections require strong coordination, continuous consultation, and mutual support among institutions charged with safeguarding democracy, peace, security, and the rule of law,” said Ethekon. The Chairperson further emphasized that the success of the 2027 General Election will largely depend on how effectively institutions coordinate and collaborate today. He reaffirmed the IEBC’s commitment to working closely with the Ministry of Interior and National Administration, development partners, and all relevant stakeholders to ensure peaceful, transparent, credible, and inclusive elections. #16thJulyByelections #YourVoteYourFuture #TalkWithIEBC #StopFakeNews

English: Public Notice: No Photos or Videos Allowed Inside Polling Booths14th May 2026. Public Notice DO NOT take Photos or Record videos in the Polling Booth. The secrecy and sanctity of the vote must be preserved at all times. Photography and Video Recording is strictly PROHIBITED in the POLLING BOOTH. Doing so constitutes an election offence under Section 7(3)(e) of the Election Offences Act, No. 37 of 2016. Section 7(3)(e) of the Election Offences Act states that a person attending any proceedings relating to an election who, without lawful excuse, captures an image of any marked ballot for purposes of financial gain or for showing allegiance, commits an offence. The offence is punishable by: a fine not exceeding KSh 1 million, or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 3 years, or both. #14thMayByelections #16thJulyByelections #YourVoteYourFuture #TalkWithIEBC #StopFakeNews

English: IEBC Vice Chairperson Fahima Araphat Abdallah, OGW, Leads IEBC Team in 2027 Budget Presentation to JLAC14th May 2026. The Commission, led by Vice Chairperson Fahima Araphat Abdallah, OGW, appeared before the National Assembly Departmental Committee on Justice and Legal Affairs (JLAC) on May 12th 2026, chaired by Hon. George Gitonga Murugara, to present the 2027 General Election budget, implementation status for the FY 2025/26 budget, project information, proposed new projects and pending bills. The Vice-Chairperson emphasized that credible elections require more than ballot papers, highlighting the importance of logistics, ICT systems, transport, ballot boxes and other operational services. Further, she observed that stakeholder engagements with diverse groups across the country is essential for electoral preparedness ahead of the 2027 General Election. She explained that different forums are required for youth, persons with disabilities, marginalized communities, and constituency-based stakeholders. The Commission also confirmed that simulation exercises and testing of election technology had been budgeted for to ensure adequate preparedness. Other activities include Enhanced Continuous Voter Registration - Phase Two, expansion of diaspora voter registration to more countries, procurement of additional Kenya Integrated Management System kits, and geospatial mapping of new polling stations in response to growth in the register of voters. JLAC members urged the Commission to have clear electoral timelines and timely reforms. In response, the Commission stated that all timelines had been incorporated into the Electoral Operations Plan and Strategic Plan, which are to be launched in June 2026 following stakeholder validation. The Committee assured the Commission of its support, while emphasizing the need for timely preparations, cost efficiency and value for public funds. #14thMayByelections #16thJulyByelections #YourVoteYourFuture #TalkWithIEBC #StopFakeNews

English: IEBC Commissioner Prof. Francis Aduol Strengthens Voter Registration Drive in Migori25th Apr 2026. Huduma Centre–based voter registration has emerged as a key milestone in the ongoing voter registration drive. During his visit to Migori County, IEBC Commissioner Prof. Francis Aduol engaged with clerks and officials overseeing the Enhanced Continuous Voter Registration (ECVR), including those stationed at the Huduma Centre in Migori Town. As part of his backstopping tour of Migori county, Prof. Aduol paid courtesy calls to the County Governor Prof. Ochilo Ayacko as well as the County Commissioner Mr. Kisilu Mutua. Both leaders affirmed their commitment to mobilizing all available resources and administrative structures to ensure that every eligible voter is reached and encouraged to register. The Commissioner also held discussions with various stakeholders, including boda boda operators, who pledged to promote peace and encourage full participation in the electoral process. English: IEBC Commissioner Dr. Ann Nderitu, CBS Calls for Public Trust and Institutional Strengthening at ICS Conference25th Apr 2026. IEBC Commissioner Dr. Ann Nderitu, CBS attended the Institute of Certified Secretaries (ICS) 30th Annual International Conference in Mombasa, themed “Resilient Governance for Thriving Economies.” Commissioner Dr. Ann took part in a panel discussion on rebuilding public trust in electoral institutions, alongside JLAC’s Chairperson Hon. George Gitonga Murugara, CBS (MP for Tharaka Constituency), Senior Counsel Charles Kanjama, President of the Law Society of Kenya (LSK), and Amb. FCS Dr. Koki Muli Grignon. Dr. Ann likened the electoral process to the role of a midwife, explaining that just as a midwife ensures the safe delivery of a child without determining the gender, the Commission facilitates the electoral process without influencing the outcome. This, she noted, underscores the Commission's commitment to delivering a transparent, credible, free, fair and inclusive electoral process. She highlighted the importance of shared responsibility in protecting electoral institutions. While public scrutiny is necessary, sustained attacks on institutions can weaken public confidence and hinder their effectiveness. She urged Kenyans to foster patience and trust in institutional processes while continuing to demand accountability. Dr. Ann also stressed the need to strengthen institutional capacity through continuous staff training, adequate resourcing and proper management of the Register of Voters (RoV) and election materials. She added that sufficient funding is critical, as elections are resource-intensive and require proper financial support to ensure effective implementation. She concluded by underscoring that credible elections depend on collaboration among all electoral stakeholders, including the government, the electoral body, voters, citizens, inter alia. She noted that such collaboration would ensure that IEBC delivers transparent, inclusive, free, fair elections, which are key to building public trust and strengthening democracy. #ECVR2026 #YourVoteYourFuture #14thMayByelections #TalkWithIEBC #StopFakeNews

English: IEBC Commissioner Hassan Noor Hassan, EBS Rallies Voters in Tharaka Nithi and Meru Ahead of ECVR Deadline21st Apr 2026. With 7 days in the offing to the conclusion of the 2026 Enhanced Continuous Voter Registration (ECVR) exercise, IEBC Commissioner Hassan Noor Hassan held stakeholder engagements in Tharaka Nithi and Meru Counties, calling on eligible voters to register before the fast-approaching deadline of Tuesday 28th April 2026. Commissioner Hassan met the security leadership led by County Commissioner (CC)Tharaka Nithi County, David Kitonga and Deputy County Commissioner (DCC) Chuka, Benson Karani who reiterated their assured security support to the IEBC team, electoral materials and activities throughout the electoral cycle. “You’re currently located in a Church, hopefully, in the near future, we can work with the Returning Officer to see if we could move IEBC premises to a secured area, to enhance your security,” said CC Kitonga. Separately, County Commissioner of Meru, Jacob Ouma called on residents to collect identification cards at their offices, saying that many remain uncollected, directly affecting their eligibility to register as voters. On his part Commissioner Hassan emphasised the need of intensified security as the General Elections draw near. “Peaceful elections are 70% security dependant, continue supporting our staff in security related matters, identify hot spots and create early warnings.Ensure all polling stations are protected, safety of staff taken seriously. Create a situation room,” Commissioner Hassan said. As the Chairperson of Human Resources (HR) and Administration Committee, Commissioner Hassan met staff based in the two counties, assuring them of continued support and assured security during the entire electoral cycle. “The Commission is looking into pertinent HR issues that have been left unattended for a while: we value your input and dedication to the electoral cause.” #ECVR2026 #YourVoteYourFuture #14thMayByelections #TalkWithIEBC #StopFakeNews

English: Commissioner Dr. Ann Nderitu CBS Calls for Gender-Responsive Electoral Processes at Legislative Summit16th Apr 2026. Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission(IEBC) , represented by Commissioner Dr. Ann Nderitu, CBS, is participating in the 6th County Assemblies Legislative Summit themed “Resilient County Assemblies: Reinforcing Representation, Legislation, and Oversight,” from 13th to 17th April 2026 in Mombasa County. The Summit, convened by the County Assemblies Forum (CAF), brought together stakeholders to strengthen legislative, representation, and oversight capacities across Kenya’s 47 County Assemblies. Presenting during General Session V on fair and inclusive elections, Commissioner Ann emphasized the need for gender-responsive planning, preparedness, and risk management in electoral processes. She noted that although women form a larger share of the population and often record higher voter turnout, they remain underrepresented in the voter register and elective positions. She called for continuous review of the register to ensure inclusivity. The Commissioner identified key barriers to women’s participation, including limited access to timely electoral information, financial constraints, and persistent societal biases. Many women, she observed, receive election information late due to competing responsibilities, underscoring the need for targeted civic and voter education. Commissioner Ann also raised concern over gender-based electoral violence, including cyberbullying and online harassment, which continue to discourage women from seeking leadership. She called for stronger measures to ensure safety and a level playing field. In conclusion, she emphasized that inclusive elections require collective action, calling on all stakeholders including men to support women’s participation and leadership in electoral processes. She also urged political parties to be more intentional in supporting women candidates through fair nomination processes and equitable placement. #ECVR2026 #YourVoteYourFuture #14thMayByelections #TalkWithIEBC #StopFakeNews

English: Commissioner Dr. Alutalala Leads ECVR Backstopping Mission to Boost Registration in Vihiga County16th Apr 2026. Commissioner Dr. Alutalala Mukhwana undertook an Enhanced Continuous Voter Registration (ECVR) backstopping visit in Vihiga County to review progress and gather feedback on ongoing voter registration efforts. During the visit, he met with Vihiga County Commissioner Peter Maina and County Police Commander Daniel Chirchir, who pledged full administrative and security support to ensure a peaceful and effective registration exercise. Dr. Alutalala also held discussions with the IEBC Vihiga County team led by Hudson Salonei, Ag. County Elections Manager, who highlighted key operational challenges including voter apathy and low collection of national ID cards, among others. The IEBC Vihiga County team also convened a stakeholder engagement meeting that brought together representatives from across the county, including youth, women, and persons with disabilities (PWDs), as well as state and non-state actors, NGAO, media, and community representatives. The forum provided a platform for inclusive dialogue, feedback, and strengthened collaboration in support of the ECVR exercise. The County Commissioner, who was present during the meeting, assured the IEBC team of targeted interventions, particularly through strengthened collaboration with chiefs in Vihiga County to ensure that uncollected IDs are issued so that young people can register as voters. He emphasized improved inter-agency coordination, enhanced field support, and continuous feedback mechanisms to boost voter registration and ensure Vihiga County meets its target for new registered voters. #ECVR2026 #YourVoteYourFuture #14thMayByelections #TalkWithIEBC #StopFakeNews

English: CLARIFICATION7th Apr 2026. Should those who registered before 2012 as voters need to register afresh? Not at all UNLESS they DID NOT register as voters from 2012 when the new Register of Voter (ROV) was established under the new Constitution of Kenya 2010 and boundaries delimitation of 2012. REASON? Because before 2012, the ROV was manual. In 2012, it went BIOMETRIC and so all eligible Kenyans were required to enrol and their Biometrics captured. This is the ROV that has been in place since 2013. As of the 2022 General Election, the Commission maintained an accurate and audited register comprising 22,120,458 voters. So we have not asked ALL OLD VOTERS PRE-2012 to register a fresh. Just those few who might have missed to register in 2012 and who, subsequently, have never registered under the Biometric system to date. No panic.!! Hapa kazi tu! Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission(IEBC) is Inclusive and Participatory as we deepen Kenya’s Democracy. #ECVR2026 #YourVoteYourFuture #14thMayByelections #TalkWithIEBC #StopFakeNews

English: IEBC Takes Voter Registration Drive to Mombasa Residents Through Stakeholder Engagement2nd Apr 2026. Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) Mombasa County Office, in conjunction with the County Government of Mombasa, held a joint stakeholder engagement on the Enhanced Continuous Voter Registration (ECVR) at Mama Ngina Waterfront. The event provided a platform for IEBC to sensitize residents of Mombasa on the ongoing ECVR exercise, which was launched on 30th March 2026 and will run until 28th April 2026. The exercise has brought voter registration services closer to the people, with IEBC staff deployed at the ward level to enhance accessibility and convenience for all eligible voters. During the event, IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon, HSC, underscored the importance of collaboration between the Commission and county governments in strengthening democratic processes and enhancing public trust. He noted that the ECVR exercise marks a critical step in expanding voter access and inclusion, particularly among youth, women, persons with disabilities, and marginalized groups. The Chairperson called on all stakeholders to actively mobilize their communities to register as voters, emphasizing that civic responsibility begins with registration and that every voice and every vote counts. He reaffirmed IEBC’s commitment to delivering a more inclusive, transparent, and credible electoral process through sustained partnerships and public engagement. The forum was graced by H.E. Abdulswamad Sheriff Nassir, Governor of Mombasa County, who urged residents to take advantage of the ongoing registration exercise and ensure they are captured in the voters’ register. He commended IEBC for decentralizing services and making them more accessible to the people of Mombasa. He noted that a significant number of eligible voters in the county are yet to register and emphasized the need for collective effort to change this. #ECVR2026 #YourVoteYourFutureYourVoice #TalkWithIEBC #StopFakeNews

English: Launch of ECVR30th Mar 2026. Today Monday 30th March 2026, the Commission is launching a nationwide Enhanced Continuous Voter Registration drive that shall run up to Tuesday 28th April 2026. The launch is happening at Shimoni Village – Old Jetty Grounds (Shimoni Fish Port) in Lunga Lunga Constituency in Kwale County. The exercise targets new registration for all, transfers and change of particulars. The #ECVR2026 exercise will be conducted at the County Assembly Wards (CAW) on a rotational basis in accordance with approved kit movement schedules as well as Institutions of Higher Learning, Huduma Ceners, Constituency Offices, Huduma Centers, and at the Commission’s Customer Experience Center (Ground Floor, Anniversary Towers). The ward-based decentralization ECVR is shifting registration from constituency offices to the ward levels to reduce travel distances for citizens in remote and rural areas. There will be a minimum of three kits per ward to ensure universal basic coverage and an additional kit will be deployed to constituencies where projected registration targets exceed their monthly capacity. Registration is open to Kenyan citizens who have attained the age of eighteen (18) years and are in possession of a valid Kenyan Passport and National Identity Card. Continuous voter registration and revision of the register shall NOT be undertaken in electoral areas with scheduled By-Elections or ongoing election petitions. #ECVR2026 #YourVoteYourFutureYourVoice #TalkWithIEBC #StopFakeNews

English: IEBC Engages MMAU to Strengthen Inclusion of Marginalised Communities in Elections26th Mar 2026. Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission(IEBC , led by Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon, HSC, held a consultative meeting with the Minority and Marginalised Affairs Unit (MMAU). The meeting also discussed areas of collaboration between the IEBC and MMAU aimed at enhancing voter education, accessing voter registration services for the minorities and marginalised groups. The Director of MMAU, Hon. Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission(IEBC) today, led by Deputy Commission Secretary - Support Services, Obadiah Keitany, MBS, officially kicked off a 3-day Training for Huduma Centre Voter Registration Clerks at the Kenya School of Government. English: IEBC, ELGIA Lead Multi-Sectoral Effort to Strengthen Electoral Legal Framework18th Mar 2026. Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission(IEBC) with support from Elgia, convened a multi-sectoral workshop in February 2026 bringing together key stakeholders to deliberate on the proposed electoral legal reforms. The engagement provided a platform for harmonizing reform proposals, refining stakeholder submissions and enhancing the overall coherence of the intended amendments to the electoral legal framework. Building on the progress achieved during that session, the Commission has now convened a two-day drafting workshop aimed at concluding the consensus building process aimed at contributing to a more robust, transparent, and credible electoral legal framework. This workshop will focus on aligning the proposals, finalizing the drafting of the amendment bill, and preparing corresponding draft regulations ahead of formal submission to Parliament for consideration. English: IEBC Hosts Lesotho Electoral Commission for Benchmarking Study Tour18th Mar 2026. The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) today hosted a delegation from the Independent Electoral Commission of Lesotho on a study tour to benchmark electoral processes. The delegation, led by Dr. Chelete Monyane, was received by IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon , who emphasized the importance of collaboration among electoral bodies to share experiences, address challenges, and strengthen electoral systems. The Commission made presentations on key areas, including legal and institutional frameworks, voter register management, results transmission, and the use of ICT in electoral processes. The delegation also expressed interest in managing complex elections, seat allocation for special interest groups and risk management strategies. They further sought to understand how the Commission manages multiple elections simultaneously up to six compared to their context, where only two are conducted. The delegation will also engage with key stakeholders, including political parties, relevant parliamentary committees, and the judiciary, to gain a broader understanding of Kenya’s electoral ecosystem. The Commission reaffirmed its commitment to continued collaboration and knowledge sharing, with both institutions expressing optimism about strengthening democratic processes across the continent. #ECVR2026 #YourVoteYourVoice #TalkWithIEBC #StopFakeNews

Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) a, led by Chairperson Erastus Ethekon, HSC today hosted a delegation from Governance Hub Africa, headed by Executive Director Brenda Isabel, in a courtesy call aimed at introducing their work and exploring strategic areas of collaboration. English: Commissioner Dr. Alutalala Highlights IEBC Voter Education Efforts on Ingo FM17th Mar 2026. Today, Commissioner Dr. Alutalala Mukhwana Chairperson Voter Education, Partnerships, Communication & Stakeholder Engagement Committee, was live on IngoFM during the morning breakfast programme dubbed Mumabwibwi where he discussed Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission(IEBC) voter education strategies. Additional kits will be assigned based on a constituency's population targets and geographical size,” said Dr. Alutalala. English: Commission Prepares for ECVR with Structured Nationwide Training Programme16th Mar 2026. In preparation for the upcoming Enhanced Continuous Voter Registration (ECVR) scheduled to begin on 30th March 2026, the Commission has adopted a structured cascaded training model. The training process begins with development of content by Master Trainers, followed by the Training of Trainers (ToTs), and culminates in cluster-level operational training for Registration Officers, Assistant Registration Officers, and temporary registration officials who will carry out the registration exercise during the ECVR. While officially opening the workshop on behalf of the Chairman, IEBC Vice Chairperson Fahima Araphat Abdallah, OGW, emphasized that the Commission’s processes must remain customer-centric to ensure the development of an accurate, inclusive, and comprehensive register of voters, which is an essential foundation for credible elections. The ECVR marks a deliberate shift from routine office-based registration to a decentralized, ward-level outreach approach. Through this strategy, the Commission will deploy additional voter registration kits, and employ Voter Registration Assistants, Voter Registration Clerks and ICT Clerks. English: IEBC Appears Before JLAC to Consider 2026 Budget Policy Statement25th Feb 2026. The Commission, led by IEBC Vice Chairperson Fahima Araphat, OGW, appeared before the Departmental Committee on Justice and Legal Affairs (JLAC) at Bunge Towers to consider the 2026 Budget Policy Statement (BPS). Vice Chairperson Araphat emphasized to the Committee that timely and sufficient funding is critical to protecting the integrity, efficiency and credibility of Kenya’s electoral process as the country prepares for the 2027 General Election. During the session, IEBC Ag. Commission Secretary/CEO Moses Sunkuli, OGW, presented the Commission’s budget priorities and strategic focus as preparations begin for the 2027 General Election. In his remarks, the CEO noted that the Commission developed its 2026/27 to 2028/29 Medium Term Expenditure Framework Budget in line with the National Treasury Circular that provides guidelines for the preparation of the 2026/27 to 2028/29 MTEF. He added that the budget is anchored on the Commission’s five year Strategic Plan, structured around four Key Result Areas and Strategic Focus Areas: Managing Elections, Citizen Engagement and Participation, Equitable Representation and Institutional Resilience. He further explained that the Commission operates under a single core programme, Management of the Electoral Process in Kenya, whose strategic objective is to deliver free, fair and credible elections. The programme is executed through five sub programmes: Administrative Planning and Support Services; Voter Registration and Electoral Operations; Voter Education and Partnerships; Electoral Information and Communication Technology; and Delimitation of Electoral Units. The Committee, chaired by Hon. George Murugara, MP for Tharaka, is established under National Assembly Standing Order 216 and is mandated to investigate, inquire into and report on matters relating to the mandate, management, activities, administration and operational estimates of designated Ministries and Departments. #26thFebByelections | #YourVoteYourFuture | #TalkwithIEBC | #StopFakeNews

English: IEBC, ELGIA Spearhead Multi Sector Electoral Law Reforms to Strengthen 2027 Polls18th Feb 2026. Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) led by Commissioner MaryKaren Sorobit, Chairperson, Legal Compliance and Political Parties Liaison Committee, in collaboration with ELGIA, is engaging stakeholders in a comprehensive electoral legal reform initiative aimed at fortifying governance and ensuring integrity in the electoral process ahead of the 2027 General Election. Describing the initiative as a key milestone in the post-2022 reform journey, Sorobit noted that the process builds on gaps identified after the 2017 General Election and reflects the Commission’s sustained commitment to strengthening the legal, administrative and regulatory framework underpinning Kenya’s elections. The reform package covers proposed amendments to the Elections Act, Election Offences Act, County Governments Act, campaign financing laws, a proposed Referendum Bill and regulations governing voter registration, voter education, party primaries and lists, election technology and campaign financing. “This is not a narrow legislative adjustment, but a structural effort to reinforce electoral governance, close legal gaps, and enhance enforceability well ahead of 2027,” she emphasized. A Multi-Sectoral Working Group, including representatives from the Kenya Law Reforms Commission, ORPP, AG, PPLC, JCE, PPDT, The National Assembly, Katiba Institute, ELOG, Transparency International, ICJ, has been established to guide the consultations and public participation process aimed at refining the draft Bills. By promoting collaboration among key election stakeholders, the Commission aims to ensure that the proposals are well-informed and aligned with the legal framework. The team is expected to fast-track the refinement and submission of the legislative instruments to Parliament in good time before the 2027 General Election. BonMak Olwal, Program Manager, UKAID, representing ELGIA, reaffirmed support for strengthening democratic governance through collaborative reform and urged stakeholders to actively contribute to enriching the proposed laws. #26thFebByelections | #YourVoteYourFuture | #TalkwithIEBC | #StopFakeNews

English: IEBC hosts a pivotal joint workshop on Election Campaign Financing and the Leadership and Integrity Framework12th Feb 2026. The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), with support from Transparency International - Kenya hosted a pivotal joint workshop on Election Campaign Financing and the Leadership and Integrity Framework. The workshop had representatives from key organizations including EACC, Commission on Administrative Justice (Office of the Ombudsman), Judiciary Committee on Elections, National Cohesion and Integration Commission, ELGIA, Katiba Institute, KNCHR, ODPP, PPLC, ELOG and ORPP. In particular, the workshop focused on finalizing amendments to Election Campaign Financing Regulations and developing a robust framework for leadership and integrity, particularly in electoral conduct, management, and participation. Chapter 6 of the Constitution mandates leadership and integrity standards, with the IEBC playing a central role in ensuring candidates meet constitutional and statutory requirements. In addition, the workshop established strategies for operationalizing the Election Campaign Financing Regulations, clarifying roles and responsibilities of stakeholders in monitoring and enforcing Chapter 6 on leadership and integrity, strengthening coordination among institutions responsible for leadership and integrity, and identifying areas for policy, legislative, or operational improvements

English: IEBC and Nation Media Group Discuss Collaboration on Responsible Electoral Reporting5th Feb 2026. Today, Nation Media Group led by its Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Mr. Geoffrey Odundo, paid a courtesy call to the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission(IEBC) to discuss areas of collaboration ahead of the 2027 General Election. Speaking during the engagement, IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon , emphasized the importance of responsible electoral communication, noting that while transparency and public-interest reporting are essential, messaging must be handled carefully to maintain public trust and participation. “As a public institution, we do not shy away from reporting legitimate issues. However, the framing and amplification of certain matters can sometimes unintentionally discourage voter participation or weaken confidence in the electoral process,” said Ethekon. The Chairperson highlighted challenges in mobilising resources for voter education and peace campaigns, observing that perceptions of adequate funding often limit support for critical communication initiatives. “To deliver a peaceful and credible election, we must invest deliberately in voter education and peace building. This cannot be achieved by the Commission alone and must be a collective national effort,” he said. The Chairperson observed there was need for a cooperative framework involving the media, civil society, and the private sector to jointly support phased peace and civic education initiatives, with the Commission committing to play its part. Mr. Odundo reiterated Nation Media Group’s civic responsibility to inform the public accurately and responsibly, describing the media as an “underwriter of democracy.” He expressed interest in collaborating with the Commission on civic education, timely dissemination of information, and effective results transmission to enhance public confidence during elections. The meeting ended by underscoring the importance of sustained collaboration in safeguarding Kenya’s stability as we prepare for the 2027 General Election. #26thFebByElections #TalkwithIEBC #StopFakeNews #YourVoteYourFuture

English: Commission Presents 2027 Election Readiness Framework to Members of Parliament28th Jan 2026. The Commission led by the IEBC Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon, HSC, made a presentation at the 2026 Legislative Retreat for Members of the National Assembly in Naivasha. The four-day retreat brings together Members of the National Assembly, led by the Speaker of the House, Rt. Hon. (Dr.) Moses Wetang'ula, to reflect on progress made, address emerging challenges, and strategize for the Fifth Session of the Thirteenth Parliament. IEBC Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon, HSC delivered a presentation on IEBC Election Management and Preparedness for the 2027 General Election, including the legislative and regulatory requirements necessary for conducting the next General Election, the budgetary and financial support required by the Commission, stakeholder support, and updates on election operations and the boundary delimitation exercise. “The Commission’s preparations for the 2027 General Election are deliberate and firmly grounded in evidence and experience. The credibility of the electoral process will depend on institutional readiness, effective inter-agency coordination, timely and adequate resourcing, and sustained public confidence,” said the Chairperson. He appreciated the National Assembly’s continued engagement and support in advancing Kenya’s democratic governance. “We recognize Parliament’s central role not only in appropriation and oversight, but also as a strategic partner in safeguarding electoral integrity, political stability, and public confidence in democratic institutions. We believe today’s engagement will foster a better understanding of the Commission’s work and strengthen institutional collaboration,” said the Chairperson. The Commission remains resolute in discharging its constitutional mandate and looks forward to Parliament’s continued partnership in upholding and protecting Kenya’s democratic architecture. English: IEBC to support women bridge gender gap in elective positions during 2027GE23rd Dec 2025. The Commission, represented by Vice Chairperson Fahima Araphat Abdallah, OGW, last week, joined the Association of Media Women in Kenya (AMWIK) and the Friedrich Naumann Foundation Kenya(FNF-Kenya) to launch a research report titled: “Bridging the Gender Gap Towards Kenya’s 2027 Elections.” The report in its findings, noted that despite the transformative aspirations of the 2010 Constitution, women currently hold only 23.9% of parliamentary seats well below the constitutional threshold. The findings underscored the reality that structural, economic, social, and digital barriers continue to undermine full representation. A key concern raised was the growing wave of online harassment targeting women leaders, journalists and human rights defenders, an area requiring collective and sustained action as the country approach the 2027 General Election. In her remarks, the Vice Chairperson reaffirmed the Commission’s commitment to supporting free, fair, inclusive and gender-responsive electoral processes

English: Commission hosts Lesotho Ministry of Justice and Law delegation benchmarking on poll management13th Dec 2025. The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), led by Chairperson Erastus Ethekon, was honored to host a delegation from the Ministry of Justice and Law of the Kingdom of Lesotho who were in the country for a benchmarking mission. The delegation’s objective is to share and learn lessons on best practices in management of elections; specifically, management of referenda and the Constitutional reform process. The Commission pointed out the need for continuous stakeholder engagements as a major area in ensuring that electoral processes are participatory, transparent and inclusive. The Lesotho team was impressed on the clear distinction of roles for different players in the democratic and electoral processes, and applauded the Commission’s commitment to openly share information and engage members of the public on its processes. The meeting was attended by IEBC Commissioners, as well as the Commission’s top management who shared their roles, responsibilities, experiences and lessons learned in the management of elections and referenda

English: IEBC evaluates election legal reforms to guide conduct of 2027 General Election13th Dec 2025. The Commission, in partnership with the Electoral Law and Governance Institute for Africa (ELGIA), last week convened a retreat to evaluate ongoing electoral legal reforms, and electoral boundary delimitation in light of the recent Supreme Court advisory. While opening the workshop, IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon, HSC underscored that the integrity of elections depends on a strong and predictable legal framework, urging Parliament to fast‐track the enactment of key electoral laws well ahead of the next General Election. The retreat is focused on examining reform proposals aimed at enhancing the efficiency, transparency, accountability, and institutional responsiveness of electoral management processes in Kenya

English: IEBC undertakes capacity building for Training of Trainers ahead of by-elections4th Dec 2025. The Commission trained Trainers of Trainers (ToTs) for the 27th November 2025 by-elections. Opening the training on behalf of the Chairperson, the Vice Chairperson Fahima Araphat Abdallah, OGW encouraged participants to continue with the same spirit and zeal of ensuring the delivery of free, fair and credible elections in the country. This will not only enhance public trust, but also strengthen Kenya’s democracy. Further, she urged poll officials to ensure all activities are guided by the rule of law and to involve stakeholders in the relevant activities to ensure a seamless electoral process. Commissioner Ann Nderitu, Chairperson of Electoral Operations Committee, requested the participants to be committed during the training as their engagement would automatically affect how the upcoming by elections are conducted and perceived by the public. Commission Secretary/CEO Marjan Hussein Marjan observed that training of poll officials remains a central pillar of quality in electoral service delivery. He also noted that during the training, attention was given to operational preparedness; pre-polling, polling and post polling activities; polling procedures, use of electronic voter identification, result management and adherence to legal and regulatory frameworks

English: IEBC undertakes capacity building for Commissioners to enhance understanding of polling process ahead of by-elections11th Nov 2025. The Commission undertook capacity building for Chairperson, Vice Chairperson and members of the Commission on electoral processes in a special workshop hosted in Mombasa.. The capacity building session, organized by the Directorate of Electoral Operations through the Electoral Training Departmen, was meant to enlighten the Commissioners to diligently deliver on IEBC Constitutional mandate, one of them being the forthcoming 24 by-elections set to be conducted on 27th November 2025 across the country. Commission Secretary/CEO Marjan Hussein Marjan emphasised the importance of Commissioners understanding the electoral process.. “We’re now delving into the mechanics of our work: how elections and referenda are conducted, how voter registration is managed, how technology enhances these processes and how all these elements combine to ensure credible elections.”. Commissioner Anne Nderitu, CBS who is the Chairperson of the Electoral Operations Committee, encouraged the trainees to carefully interrogate the presentations as it is the backbone of election management. She emphasized that the Commission has a rich knowledge base to deliver the tailored content.. During the closing ceremony, the Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon, HSC expressed satisfaction with the Commission’s internal trainers. He encouraged the CEO to institutionalize a knowledge management centre to facilitate ongoing knowledge transfer and experience sharing within the Commission.. Further, the Chairperson urged the Commission to expand training to external stakeholders in the electoral sector, ensuring they remain well-informed and actively engaged with the electoral sub-system.. The customised training was designed to equip the Commissioners with hands-on knowledge and experience in electoral-legal framework, voter registration, conduct of elections, results management, election technology, stakeholder engagement, communication among others. These initiatives underscore the Commission’s dedication to enhance public trust and strengthen Kenya’s democracy

English: Commission pays tribute to former Prime Minister Raila Odinga as he takes final bow out of Kenyas political landscape27th Oct 2025. The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) bows its head in deep sorrow and solemn respect at the passing of His Excellency, The Rt. Hon. Raila Amolo Odinga - a statesman of rare courage, patriot of unmatched devotion, and steadfast architect of Kenya’s democracy. The Chairperson, Members and Staff of the Commission extend their heartfelt condolences to the Odinga family, and to a nation united in grief. Kenya has lost a towering son whose voice, vision, and valour shaped its destiny. The Rt. Hon. Odinga’s indomitable spirit guided our nation through its most defining moments - from the struggle for multiparty democracy, to the birth of the 2010 Constitution; and relentless quest for credible, transparent and people-centered elections. His sacrifices strengthened the institutions that uphold the sovereign will of the Kenyan people. Indeed, his life is etched in our democratic foundations - in every reform, every freedom and every ballot cast. For this, we owe him a debt of eternal gratitude. In his honour, the IEBC rededicates itself to his vision - to defend integrity, impartiality, and transparency in every election, and to ensure that the voice of every Kenyan remains sacred and supreme. Go well, Great Son of Kenya. Your dream for a just, democratic and united nation will forever inspire our path

English: Commission visits Mashuuru Primary Boarding School, engages students and gives back to community in CSR gesture20th Oct 2025. As part of its ongoing Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiatives, the Commission organized a community outreach activity at Mashuuru Boarding Primary School in Kajiado County during the launch of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise held on 29th September 2025. The school, being one of the polling stations used by the Commission, was selected to benefit from this initiative in recognition of its long-standing partnership with the IEBC in facilitating electoral activities. The CSR activity was led by the Deputy Commission Secretary – Operations, Ruth Kulundu, and the Deputy Commission Secretary – Support Services, Obadiah Keitany. The event aimed to give back to the community, promote education, and strengthen the Commission’s relationship with local residents. During the activity, the Commission donated various essential items to the school, including stationery to enhance learning, sanitary towels to promote menstrual hygiene and support girls’ education, footballs to encourage cocurricular activities, and school bags to motivate pupils and foster community development. In addition, the IEBC team planted 20 trees within the school compound as part of its commitment to environmental conservation and sustainability. The tree-planting exercise symbolized the Commission’s dedication to nurturing not only democracy but also a greener, healthier future for communities across the country. Through this CSR initiative, the Commission demonstrated its commitment to education, youth empowerment, and community development

English: IEBC develops Medium-Term Expenditure Framework, pledges to observe prudent financial planning and accountability20th Oct 2025. The Commission led by Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon, HSC, convened at the serane Sawela Lodges in Naivasha from 22nd to 26th September 2025 to develop its Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF) for the financial years 2026/27, 2027/28, and 2028/29. The Chaiperson observed that at the heart of the budget preparation process is a commitment to prudent financial planning, expenditure and accountability guaranteeing value for money while enhancing service delivery. While opening the workshop, Ethekon noted: “History reminds us that credible elections are not born on Election Day. They are built here in strategic meetings like this, where planning meets responsibility.” The Chairperson underscored the need for integrity in budgeting and to help the country manage election costs by optimizing scarce resources without compromising quality. “When we work on these numbers, they must not be arbitrary. Every proposal must be realistic, rational and aligned with our institutional goals. The budget we shape here is not just about figures it is the blueprint for building trust, credibility and confidence in our electoral process,” said Ethekon. The Commission’s Vice-Chairperson, Ms. Fahima Araphat Abdallah, OGW, who chairs the Finance & Procurement Committee, emphasized that the workshop marks the foundation of financial planning and electoral readiness for the next three years. She emphasized on the need to create a budget that complies with National Treasury circular, supports IEBC operations, reflects economic realities, and upholds the Commission’s constitutional mandate. The 10th August 2027 General Election falls within the current MTEF and the Commission has begun engaging the National Treasury as well as committees of parliament to ensure timely planning, allocation and disbursement of funds for the preparation and management of elections

English: Commission targets 6.3 million new voters on resumption of Continuous Voter Registration exercise29th Sep 2025. The Commission Chairperson, Erastus Edung Ethekon, has assured the public that IEBC is fully prepared and working diligently for the forthcoming by-elections as a precursor to the 2027 General Election. He emphasized that preparations for the by-elections are on course. On resumption of Continuous Voter Registration, the Chairperson stated that the Commission aims to enlist 6.3 million new eligible voters, 70 percent of whom are youth. This assurance came during his appearance before the Parliamentary Accounts Committee, led by Butere Member of the National Assembly Hon. Tindi Mwale, where the Commission had been invited to respond to the Auditor General’s report on Account of the National Government for the Financial year ended 30th June 2023. The Chairperson also pledged to maintain close collaboration with the leadership of both houses of Parliament and the various committees, as well as other stakeholders. “We have an open-door policy and remain committed to working closely with the leadership of both houses of Parliament and all progressive Kenyans to enhance our electoral processes and voter experience,” said Ethekon

English: Commission administers Oath of Secrecy to gazetted Returning Officers ahead of by-elections29th Sep 2025. The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) ’s legal team led by Direcor of Legal Services (DLS) Chrispine Owiye, OGW on Friday, 19th September, 2025 oversaw the administration of Oath of Secrecy of the Ballot to gazetted Returning Officers and other IEBC staff at the end of a joint National Planning meeting in Naivasha. The Officers will be involved in the conduct of the 24 By-Elections across the country on 27th November 2025. The 24 By-Elections are for Member of Senate - Baringo County (1); Members of the National Assembly for Banissa, Kasipul, Magarini, Malava, Mbeere North and Ugunja Constituencies (6); Members of County Assemblies: Angata Nanyokie Ward in Samburu County, Chemundu/Kapng’etuny Ward in Nandi County, Chewani Ward in Tana River County, Fafi Ward in Garissa County and Kariobangi North Ward in Nairobi City County. Others are Kisa East Ward in Kakamega County, Metkei Ward in Elgeyo Marakwet County, Mumbuni North Ward in Machakos County, Narok Town Ward in Narok County, Purko Ward in Kajiado County, Tembelio Ward in Uasin Gishu County, Nyansiongo, Nyamaiya, Ekerenyo Wards in Nyamira County, Kabuchai/Chwele Ward in Bungoma County, Lake Zone and Nanaam Wards in Turkana County (17). The campaign period runs from 8th October 2025 and ceases on 24th November 2025, being 48 hours before the by-election day between 7:00 am and 6:00 pm. Political parties and candidates are to appoint and submit the names of their agents 14 days before the date of the by-elections to facilitate the processing of their details and training

English: Commissioner Dr. Alutalala engages media, highlights IEBC Roadmap to 2027 General Election14th Sep 2025. The Chairperson of the Voter Education, Partnerships, Communications and Stakeholder Engagement Committee, Commissioner Dr. Mukhwana Alutalala, recently appeared on several media platforms including Nation FM, Spice FM, and TV 47 to update the public on the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission’s (IEBC) preparations for the upcoming key electoral activities leading to the 2027 elections. Dr. Alutalala elaborated on the establishment of Commission Committees designed to enhance efficient coordination across various Directorates and thematic areas, supporting the effective implementation of the Commission’s Constitutional mandate. Addressing concerns over public trust and confidence in the electoral process, Commissioner Alutalala emphasized IEBC’s commitment to transparency through timely communication and continuous engagement with stakeholders. He highlighted the strategic focus on reaching young voters, who constitute over 70% of Kenya’s population, with tailored voter education and communication campaigns aimed at first-time and new voters. Dr. Alutalala acknowledged Kenya’s complex electoral history and the high stakes associated with the elections as key contributors to skepticism. However, he firmly reassured Kenyans that the current electoral management framework leaves no room for rigging, asserting that the notion of electoral theft is no longer feasible in today’s environment. To further bolster public confidence, the Commissioner announced that IEBC will conduct practical live simulation exercises in media outlets demonstrating the voting and results management processes. These simulations intend to demystify the electoral process and clearly show how it is safeguarded against any interference. Commissioner Alutalala’s media engagements reaffirm the Commission’s resolve to deliver a credible, transparent, and inclusive electoral process in 2027

English: Master trainers reviews training content for staff in readiness for resumption of Continuous Voter Registration exercise14th Sep 2025. The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) last week held a workshop to develop training content and methodology by Master Trainers ahead of the resumption of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) on 29th September, 2025. This will be followed by a comprehensive training for both field Registration Officers and support staff from the headquarters. The training will adopt a three-tier model. Tier 1 involves developing training content and methodology by Master Trainers, Tier 2 targets Training of Trainers (TOTs), and Tier 3 involves comprehensive training of field officers and support staff from headquarters. This programme will cover all aspects of the CVR process, from operational procedures to the technical nuances of the new Kenya Integrated Election Management System’s (KIEMS) voter registration module. The Commission notes that this approach will ensure consistency and standardization of electoral operations across all levels and offices of Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC). Further, it will provide uniform application of electoral laws, procedures, technologies and enhance preparedness and risk management aspects of the CVR exercise

English:
Commission engages Civil Society Organisations to build united front and strengthen electoral governance14th Sep 2025.

Last week marked a pivotal moment for Kenya’s democratic future as the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), led by Vice Chairperson Fahima Araphat Abdallah, OGW, held a high-level round-table meeting with Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) under the Uchaguzi Platform, with support from ELOG and ELGIA.

With the 2027 General Election on the horizon, the meeting aimed to build a united front between the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission and civil society to strengthen electoral governance, promote transparency, and defend the sanctity of the vote.

Vice Chair Fahima, speaking on behalf of Chairperson Erestus Edung Ethekon, emphasized the Commission’s commitment to inclusive, participatory, and accountable elections.

“Your proposals will guide the development of policy and strategy to enhance participation and restore public trust in the electoral process,” she said.

The Commission also sounded the alarm on the growing threat of misinformation and disinformation, cautioningCSOs to stay vigilant against politically driven narratives that could undermine electoral integrity and national unity.

Representatives from Uchaguzi Platform, including Felix Odhiambo from ELGIA Africa and the National Coordinator of Elog-Mulle Musau, commended IEBC’s willingness to engage and pledged full support in advancing transparency, civic engagement, and accountability.

With democracy under pressure globally, Kenya is standing tall—fighting for a future where every vote counts and every voice matters. The 2027 journey starts now—and it’s a call to all patriots to guard our ballot and defend our democracy.

English: IEBC pays courtesy call on Chief Justice, discuss areas of interest to impact 2027 GE9th Sep 2025. Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) Chairperson Erastus Ethekon and Members of the Commission on Wednesday 27th August, 2025 paid a courtesy call to the Chief Justice and President of the Supreme Court of Kenya, Hon. Lady Justice Martha Koome, EGH. The two institutions deliberated on matters of mutual interest that will impact the 2027 General Election. The Commission is seeking to strengthen mutual understanding and synergy between the two institutions and recognizes the critical role played by the Judiciary, specifically the Judiciary Committee on Elections (JCE), during the pre-election, election and post-election periods in ensuring fair and timely dispute resolution. The Chief Justice and members of the Supreme Court Hon. Justice Njoki Ndungu, CBS, who is also Chairperson of JCE, and Hon. Justice Daniel Musinga, Vice-Chairperson JCE, congratulated the IEBC Chairperson and Commissioners on their appointment to office and pledged to support them deliver on their mandate. The Chairperson noted that to strengthen the preparation for the 2027 General Election, the Commission proposes to revise electoral laws and Collaboration regulations to address challenges observed in 2017 and 2022. This will enhance collaboration with JCE to establish a more workable Electoral Dispute Resolution (EDR) framework, develop training programmes and curricula on electoral processes and dispute resolution. Further it will aid in building capacity of law enforcement agencies on electoral processes, strengthen stakeholder and government agency engagements and sensitize Judicial Officers on electoral processes, particularly the allocation of party lists

English: UN Resident Coordinator pays courtesy call on Commission, renews collaboration7th Aug 2025. A United Nations delegation led by UN Resident Coordinator Dr. Stephen Jackson and UNDP Deputy Resident Representative – Programmes Madelena Monoja paid a courtesy call to the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission(IEBC). The delegation was welcomed by Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission(IEBC) Chairperson Erastus Ethekon together with Members of the Commission and discussed a raft of programmes and activities that UNDP can support and partner with the Commission. In particular, the Chairperson discussed voter registration exercise, pending by-elections and enhancing grassroot voter education. The Chairperson acknowledged the work done by the Secretariat in drafting the 2024-2029 Strategic Plan, from which the Commission will develop the Election Operation Plan (EOP) and the Boundaries Review Operation Plan (BROP). The delegation was also apprised on the induction programme that the Commissioners were taken through where they interacted with experts in governance, law and elections. The Chairperson acclaimed the induction as informative as it highlighted the challenges encountered from previous elections and best global practices. Chairperson recognised the role UNDP plays in Kenya’s electoral process and asked the development partners to continue supporting the Commission especially in the upcoming by-elections. The delegation shared its congratulatory messages on the appointment and swearing in of the Commission and pledged to continue supporting the Commission deliver on its mandate ahead of the 2027 General Election. UN Resident Coordinator Dr. Stephen Jackson said it was a pleasure to meet the new Commission noting that UNDP has had partnership with the Commission that has endured many electoral cycles and he was glad to renew the partnership now that the new Commission was in place

English: Advance Cargo Declaration (ACD) Platform for Containerized Cargo. BACK TO PUBLIC NOTICES Advance Cargo Declaration (ACD) Platform for Containerized Cargo To: All Importers, Exporters Shipping Goods to Kenya, Shipowners, Carriers, Shipping Agents, Customs Agents, and Relevant Stakeholders. Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) informs all users of Kenya’s ports that an Advance Cargo Declaration (ACD) platform, a digital pre-arrival cargo system for all containerised cargo destined for Kenya ports is now available. The implementation of this platform will be launched on Monday, 3rd August, 2026. Exporters shipping goods to Kenya will obtain an ACD reference code from acd.kra.go.ke at the point of loading containerised cargo destined for Kenya ports. The reference code will be generated once the following documents are uploaded to the platform: 1. Draft Bill of Lading 2. Commercial Invoice 3. Freight Invoice, and 4. Export Declaration. The ACD reference code will be endorsed on the Bill of Lading before the shipment proceeds to a Kenyan port. Stakeholders are urged to visit acd.kra.go.ke for full guidance on the ACD process. For further inquiries, please email operations@acd.kra.go.ke or info@acd.kra.go.ke . English: Removal of Excise Duty on Bottled Water. BACK TO PUBLIC NOTICES Removal of Excise Duty on Bottled Water Kenya Revenue Authority notifies all licensed manufacturers and importers of bottled water and the general public that pursuant to the Finance Act, 2026 (amending the First Schedule to the Excise Duty Act, Cap 472), excise duty on bottled water is removed with effect from 1st July, 2026. Bottled water manufactured or imported on or after this date will not be subject to excise duty and will not require to be affixed with excise stamps. The Commissioner will issue detailed guidelines on the return of unutilized stamps and the decommissioning of digital stamps, which will be published on the official KRA website. Manufacturers are reminded of their obligation to submit their Excise Duty Returns for the month of June 2026 and pay the taxes due by 20th July, 2026. The eTIMS Fuel Station System is a tailored solution for the fuel sector, enabling seamless, real-time invoicing for every transaction. It integrates with KRA through a forecourt controller and existing point-of-sale systems, ensuring accuracy and efficiency in tax reporting. KRA remains committed to supporting and facilitating all fuel retailers in meeting these requirements. We also extend our appreciation to the outlets that have already complied with the electronic tax invoicing mandate. Retailers who fail to comply by 31st December, 2025 , will face enforcement measures as provided for under the law. English: Exemption of Non-Resident Suppliers of Digital Services from the VAT (Electronic Tax Invoice) Regulations, 2020. BACK TO PUBLIC NOTICES Exemption of Non-Resident Suppliers of Digital Services from the VAT (Electronic Tax Invoice) Regulations, 2020 Kenya Revenue Authority wishes to clarify to the public and all VAT registered taxpayers that the Value Added Tax (Digital Marketplace Supply) Regulations, 2020 exempts registered non-resident suppliers of digital services from issuing electronic tax invoices as required under the Value Added Tax (Electronic Tax Invoice) Regulations, 2020. However, the non-resident suppliers of digital services are required to issue invoices or receipts showing the value of the supply and the tax charged. VAT registered taxpayers in Kenya who import such services may claim the input tax so charged at the end of the tax period in which the importation occurs in line with the provisions of the VAT Act, 2013. The necessary enhancements have been made to the iTax system to support this compliance framework. English: Validation of Import Declarations in the VAT Return. BACK TO PUBLIC NOTICES Validation of Import Declarations in the VAT Return Kenya Revenue Authority would like to inform the public and taxpayers of the changes on deduction of input tax on imports. Section 17 of the VAT Act, 2013 provides for deduction of input tax on importation made by a registered person. The deduction shall be allowed from the tax payable on supplies made by the person, within six months after the end of the tax period in which the importation occurred but only to the extent that the importation was acquired to make taxable supplies. KRA therefore notifies VAT registered persons of the changes made on the VAT Return filing process. The changes involve validation of import claims against existing Customs import declarations, upon upload of the VAT return on iTax. Additional information is available on the KRA website, www.kra.go.ke . For further assistance, visit your nearest Tax Service Office. English: Insurance Relief on Contributions to National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF). Insurance Relief on Contributions to National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) Insurance Relief on Contributions to National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) Kenya Revenue Authority would like to inform all employers and members of the public that the Finance Act, 2021 amended Section 31(1) of the Income Tax Act (ITA), Cap 470 to extend the existing Insurance Relief to include contributions made to the National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF). Paragraph 2 of Head A of the Third Schedule to the ITA provides that the amount of Insurance Relief shall be fifteen percent of the amount of premiums paid but shall not exceed sixty thousand shillings per annum. Contributions to NHIF will therefore be eligible in the computation of Insurance Relief as follows: - Insurance Relief = 15% (Insurance Premiums + NHIF Contributions) but shall not exceed Kshs. 5,000.00 per month or Kshs. 60,000.00 per year. The effective date of this amendment was 1st January 2022 . COMMISSIONER FOR DOMESTIC TAXES 💬 Address Times Tower Building Haile Selassie Avenue P. O. English: Requirements for Uptake of the Electronic Tax Invoice. BACK TO PUBLIC NOTICES Requirements for Uptake of the Electronic Tax Invoice The Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) wishes to notify all VAT registered taxpayers and the public that the new Electronic Tax Registers (ETRs) that are compliant with the Tax Invoice Management System (TIMS) are now subject to an automated activation process through the iTax System. In this regard, KRA will no longer issue approval letters for the purchase of non TIMS compliant ETRs to newly VAT registered taxpayers or taxpayers intending to replace their existing ETRs. Consequently, suppliers of ETRs are notified to cease supply of Electronic Tax Registers that are not compliant with the Value Added Tax (Electronic Tax Invoice) Regulations, 2020 effective 15th January 2022. KRA takes this opportunity to thank all the VAT registered taxpayers who have come on board as early adopters and are already generating and transmitting Electronic Tax Invoices to KRA. English: Withdrawal of Ruling on Treatment of Tax Loss in Computing Profits. BACK TO PUBLIC NOTICES Withdrawal of Ruling on Treatment of Tax Loss in Computing Profits Section 15(7) of the Income Tax Act Cap. 470 requires that a person who derives income from one or more specified sources will submit a separate account and a separate computation in respect of each specified source. In line with section 64(1) of the Tax Procedures Act, KRA informs the public of the withdrawal of the waiver of this requirement granted through a letter dated 7 th February 1979 addressed to Institute of Certified Public Accountants (ICPAK), with effect from 1 st October 2021 . Henceforth, all taxpayers will be required to prepare a separate account in respect of each specified source of income and in the event of a loss, that loss may only be deducted from gains or profits of that person derived from the specified source in the following year or subsequent years of income in so far as the loss has not already been deducted. English: Automation of the Voluntary Tax Disclosure Programme. BACK TO PUBLIC NOTICES Automation of the Voluntary Tax Disclosure Programme The Finance Act, 2020 introduced a three-year Voluntary Tax Disclosure Programme (VTDP) effective 1st January 2021 to 31st December 2023. VTDP is a programme where a person upon disclosing previously undisclosed tax liabilities to the Commissioner, is granted relief from penalties and interest on the taxes disclosed. Kenya Revenue Authority wishes to inform the public that applications for grant of relief of penalties and interest under the VTDP can now be made online through the iTax portal. Successful applicants will receive VTDP certificates via their registered email addresses. Taxpayers with previously undisclosed taxes are encouraged to take advantage of the relief granted under the VTDP to avoid imposition of punitive penalties and interest. A step-by-step guide on the VTDP application process together with VTDP FAQs are available on the KRA website. English: Fringe Benefit Tax, Deemed Interest Rate and Low Interest Benefit. BACK TO PUBLIC NOTICES Fringe Benefit Tax, Deemed Interest Rate and Low Interest Benefit FRINGE BENEFIT TAX For the purposes of Section 12B of the Income Tax Act, the Market Interest Rate is 7% . This rate shall be applicable for the three months of July, August and September 2021. DEEMED INTEREST RATE For purposes of section 16(5), the prescribed rate of interest is 7% . This is applicable for the months of July, August and September 2021. LOW INTEREST BENEFIT For purposes of section 5(2A), the prescribed rate of interest is 7%. This is applicable for the months of July, August ,September, October, November and December 2021 . Withholding tax rate of 15% on the deemed interest shall be deducted and paid to the Commissioner by the 20th day of the month following the month of computation. English: Paperless Customs Clearance at the Entry and Exit Points. BACK TO PUBLIC NOTICES Paperless Customs Clearance at the Entry and Exit Points Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) wishes to notify all stakeholders that KRA is implementing paperless Customs clearance of cargo at all entry and exit points. Customs will perform paperless examination, approval and release of inbound and outbound goods through the Customs systems. This new process commenced in May 2020. Reducing paperwork during Customs clearance will facilitate transparency, increased tax compliance, simplification of international trade and reduce time and cost of doing business. KRA is committed to ensuring that the necessary support is availed to facilitate cargo clearance in the entry and exit points. All stakeholders are therefore encouraged to take up paperless cargo clearance. English: Voluntary Tax Disclosure Programme. BACK TO PUBLIC NOTICES Voluntary Tax Disclosure Programme Kenya Revenue Authority informs members of the public that the Voluntary Tax Disclosure Programme introduced vide the Finance Act 2020, shall commence on 1st January 2021 and run for three years to 31st December 2023. The Disclosure programme, allows a person to disclose to the Commissioner tax liabilities that were previously undeclared and enjoy full or partial relief of penalties and interest on the tax disclosed under the programme. It shall apply to tax liabilities accrued in the period commencing on or after 1st July 2015 but not later than 30th June 2020. Persons who are interested in obtaining relief under the Voluntary Tax Disclosure Programme shall apply through a prescribed online application form on the i-Tax system. Guidelines on the operation of the Voluntary Tax Disclosure Programme together with the step-by-step guide on the application process for the programme can be found on the Kenya Revenue Authority website. English: Importation of Excisable Goods, Cigarette Paper, Cigarette Packaging Materials and Unprocessed Tobacco. BACK TO PUBLIC NOTICES Importation of Excisable Goods, Cigarette Paper, Cigarette Packaging Materials and Unprocessed Tobacco The Excise Duty Act,2015, under Section 15, as read with The Excise Duty Regulations, 2020 and the Excise Duty (EGMS) Regulations, 2017 require that importers of the following goods acquire an excise license before importing the goods. This includes: All excisable goods, other than motor vehicle, Raw/unprocessed tobacco Cigarette paper and cigarette packaging materials. To facilitate the taxpayers, the services of licencing/registration of excise licences are now available at our Tax Service Offices across the country. Taxpayers requiring these services are encouraged to apply through the website or visit any of our Tax Service Offices. KRA informs all importers that no person will be allowed to import any of these products into the country without an excise license. Further, any goods imported in contravention of the law will be seized and forfeited. English: Licence for Conveyance of Goods under Customs Control. BACK TO PUBLIC NOTICES Licence for Conveyance of Goods under Customs Control The Commissioner of Customs and Border Control notifies all shippers, clearing agents, transporters and stakeholders in the conveyance of goods under customs control that pursuant to regulation 210 and 211 of The East Africa Community Customs Management Regulations 2010 that goods subject to customs control may only be conveyed by a vessel or vehicle licenced by the Commissioner for that purpose. All stakeholders under this category are therefore urged to familiarise themselves with the provisions of the said sections and ensure compliance within 14 days from the date of this notice. Please note that vehicles conveying transit goods and licenced under regulation 104 of the said regulations are exempted from this directive. English: Payment of Stamp Duty & Capital Gains Tax. BACK TO PUBLIC NOTICES Payment of Stamp Duty & Capital Gains Tax Kenya Revenue Authority informs the public that it is in the process of simplifying Stamp Duty payment process on the iTax system and thereby expediting the payments. Following the changes, it will no longer be conditional to present a Capital Gain Tax Acknowledgement Slip before Stamp Duty payment is processed. This reform is expected to improve the ease of doing business by creating efficiency in the process and promoting investments. KRA emphasizes that transfer of property still attracts Capital Gains Tax which is payable by the transferor on or before the 20th day of the following month in which the transfer of property is effected. For further clarification and facilitation, please contact the Contact Centre on Tel: 020 4 999 999, 0711 099 999 or Email callcentre@kra.go.ke. You may also visit the nearest KRA office. English: Migration of Legacy Ledger Balances to iTax. BACK TO PUBLIC NOTICES Migration of Legacy Ledger Balances to iTax KRA is undertaking a reconciliation exercise of the taxpayers’ accounts in the old system to establish the correct tax balances. The balances will thereafter be migrated to the new iTax system. During the exercise, taxpayers will be contacted by heads of their respective Tax Stations through letters to confirm their ledger balances before the migration. The exercise which has commenced with Large and Medium Taxpayers will in due course be rolled out to other taxpayers’ countrywide. KRA emphasizes that the communication under this exercise will be a request for confirmation of the correctness of the balances and not an assessment. English: Turnover Tax. BACK TO PUBLIC NOTICES Turnover Tax Kenya Revenue Authority would like to notify the public that in accordance with the Finance Act, 2019, the Turnover Tax (TOT) has been re-introduced and will be payable from 1st January 2020. The tax rate for TOT is 3% on the gross sales/turnover and is a final tax. TOT will be paid on a monthly basis. The due date is on or before 20th of the following month. The TOT tax does not apply to persons; with business income of Kshs 5,000,000 and above, Rental Income, Limited Liability Companies, Management and Professional Services. Eligible taxpayers are advised to log onto iTax, add the TOT obligation, file the monthly returns and make payment. English: Fringe Benefit Tax (FBT) and Deemed Interest Rate. BACK TO PUBLIC NOTICES Fringe Benefit Tax (FBT) and Deemed Interest Rate Fringe Benefit Tax For the purposes of Section 12B of the Income Tax Act, the Market Interest Rate is 6%. This rate shall be applicable for the three months of October, November and December 2019. Deemed Interest Rate For purposes of section 16(5), the prescribed rate of interest is 6%. This is applicable for the months of October, November and December 2019. Withholding tax rate of 15% on the deemed interest shall be deducted and paid to the Commissioner by 20th of the month following the month of computation. English: Automated Verification of VAT Returns. BACK TO PUBLIC NOTICES Automated Verification of VAT Returns 25th March, 2019 The Kenya Revenue Authority would wish to inform the public that system improvements made to the iTax VAT return verification module following stakeholders’ feedback, have been concluded. The module cross-validates invoice details in buyers’ and sellers’ VAT returns then generates inconsistencies which affected taxpayers are required to resolve within a given period from the date of system notification. Further, KRA wishes to advise Taxpayers that were affected by the verification of the January 2018 returns to amend their returns within 60 days from the date of this Notice.Input tax relating to inconsistencies which will remain unresolved after the stated period shall be disallowed. Taxpayers who need assistance are encouraged to seek support through KRA nationwide taxpayer support arrangement outlined in this notice. For support please liaise with the Contact Centre on Tel. 020 4999999; 0711 099999 or E-Mail address callcentre@kra.go.ke . You may also visit the nearest KRA Office, iTax Support Centre or Huduma Centre. Additional information is available on the KRA website ( www.kra.go.ke ).
