English: British High Commissioner seeks to partner with IEBC to strengthen democracy7th Aug 2025. The Commission today hosted the British High Commissioner to Kenya Neil Wigan and held a consultative meeting to discuss areas of mutual interest and collaboration to strengthen democracy. Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission(IEBC) Chairperson Erastus Ethekon together with the Members of the Commission welcomed the Head of Mission and shared IEBC’s mandate. The Commission expressed its commitment to conduct its operations in transparent manner to enhance public trust in the election process ahead of the 23 by-elections and resumption of voter registration exercise. With over 6 million youth expected to be enrolled in the register of voters, IEBC Chairperson committed to leverage on modern technology and new media to reach out to the young voters and other stakeholders and make each voice count in strengthening democracy in Kenya. The Commission will also engage stakeholders in the political space, media, development partners and experts in governance and electoral process to enhance IEBC’s capacity in delivering on its mandate

English: Commission meets PETRAD Aid discusses strategies to strengthen Voter Education5th Jun 2025. The Commission on Thursday 22nd May, 2025 hosted the board of directors from The People Transformation and Development Aid (PETRAD AID) (http://www.petradaid.org/) and discussed collaboration opportunities and areas of mutual interest. PETRAD Aid is one of the accredited organisations that collaborated with the Commission in providing voter education and election observation during the 2022 General Election. Petrad Aid team, which was led by CEO Evanson Epetet, is seeking to strengthen its support and collaboration with the Commission in the build up to the 2027 General Election. Commission Secretary/CEO, Marjan Hussein Marjan, welcomed the team and appreciated the support and effort they have made to enlighten voters on election processes, which has gone a long way to strengthen democracy in the country. “The Commission will soon place an advertisement calling on all eligible Voter Education Providers and Election Observers to apply for accreditation. This will help it coordinate voter education and link providers with potential development partners for funding to carry out the exercise,” said Marjan. Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) a Director Voter Education and Partnership Joyce Ekuam took the PETRAD Aid Board through the election processes including voter registration, boundaries delimitation and public outreach strategies. “We need to reach out to the public and preach peace and harmony. Be ambassadors of peace throughout the election cycle building strong, unified communities where everyone feels valued, respected and included, regardless of their background or differences. Let us promote a future where cooperation and collaboration lead to a more just and equitable world,” said Ekuam. Through such meetings, the Commission receives feedback from stakeholders that informs areas of improvement as it undertakes its mandate

English: IEBC revises training content for Commissioners induction course and set by-elections timelines session-class8th Apr 2025. The Commission, with support from the Electoral Law and Governance Institute for Africa (ELGIA), is conducting a four-day workshop on Development of Training Content and Methodology, and By-elections timelines. Recognising the complexity of elections and the need for specialised expertise, the Commission is developing a training programme for newly recruited Commissioners. This programme will equip them with essential knowledge for policy formulation, strategic planning, and effective oversight. Continuous training programmes will also ensure that Commission staff remain updated with the latest electoral best practices. Additionally, following the 2022 General Election, 17 electoral area vacancies have arisen due to election petitions, resignations and the passing of elected leaders. To address these vacancies and uphold democratic governance, the Commission has developed a draft By-Election Operational Plan. While opening the workshop, Moses Sunkuli, Director of Voter Registration & Electoral Operations, emphasised the urgency of detailed by-election planning, given that some vacancies have exceeded the 90-day timeline due to the absence of a Commission. “We are moving beyond basic orientation to comprehensive training that equips Commissioners with a strong understanding of electoral processes, ensuring they lead with confidence and competence,” stated Sunkuli. Representing ELGIA CEO Felix Odhiambo Odwuor, Bon MakOlwal, Senior Manager of Electoral Reforms, reinforced the need for the Commission to take ownership of the induction process to fully prepare new Commissioners for their responsibilities. “This workshop is crucial in developing a structured curriculum that will equip the new Commissioners to oversee elections effectively, especially with pending by-elections,” added MakOlwal

English: IEBC engages stakeholders in EU Electoral Follow-up Mission to strengthen elections26th Feb 2025. IEBC Led by Deputy Commission Secretary – Operations Ruth Kulundu, participated in a roundtable discussion organised by the European Union (EU) Electoral Follow-up Mission to Kenya. The forum, which was at Sankara Hotel in Nairobi, offered a platform for key electoral stakeholders to provide feedback and recommendations aimed at strengthening Kenya’s electoral processes. Members of the EU Electoral Follow-up Mission and other stakeholders engaged constructively with the IEBC team, sharing insights on challenges and opportunities for improving electoral integrity and inclusivity. Speaking at the forum, DCS Kulundu reaffirmed the Commission’s commitment to upholding free, fair, and credible elections. “Engaging with stakeholders is essential in ensuring that our electoral processes are inclusive and transparent. We welcome these recommendations and will consider them as we continue to refine our electoral framework,” said Kulundu. Stakeholders present included political parties, representatives of Persons with Disabilities, women and youth groups, the National Cohesion and Integration Commission (NCIC), the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights (KNCHR), the Media Council of Kenya, the National Council of Churches of Kenya among others. Each group shared perspectives on enhancing electoral accessibility, transparency and fairness

English: Commission submits to Parliamentary Accounts Committee on queries raised by Auditor General17th Feb 2025. On Monday 26th August, 2024, the Commission led by Chief Executive Officer Marjan Hussein Marjan submitted to the Parliamentary Accounts Committee (PAC) on various audit queries raised by the Office of the Auditor General. PAC had invited the Commission to shed light on some of the audit queries touching on various sections of the examination Report of the Auditor General on Accounts of National Government for the Financial Year Ended 30th June 2022. The PAC led by Butere Constituency legislator Tindi Mwale afforded the Commission an opportunity to respond to the matters raised in the report. The Committee wanted IEBC to respond to why it has not recovered money owed to it by debtors resulting from court awards. The CEO tabled a response saying it was to engage the services of registered auctioneers to recover the money owed. The Commission also clarified on the number of kits that had been alleged as ‘lost’ by the auditor’s report. The CEO clarified that the report referred to by the Auditor General was an internal document prepared to determine the status of the usability of the KIEMS kits as well as those that had become obsolete. The Committee granted the Commission one month to Liaise with the the Office of the Auditor General to ascertain the accurate count of the number of KIEMS kits owned by the Commission. The CEO was accompanied by the Deputy Commission Secretary Operations Ruth Kulundu, Directors and managers

English: IEBC joins International Commission of Jurists to validate 2022 election compendium23rd Aug 2024. The Commission took part in a validation forum hosted by the International Commission of Jurists (ICJ) in Nairobi on 9th August, 2024 that discussed the 2022 Election Compendium. Ruth Makuthu, the Ag. Manager Legal Reforms, Political Parties and Campaign Financing and also a member of ICJ represented the Commission, which was invited owing to its mandate to conduct elections. The Commissions provided insights on how to enhance quality of information compiled that is critical in the validation process to finalize the 2022 Election Compendium. ICJ Kenya, in partnership with Uraia Trust through the support of DANIDA, has been implementing the Electoral Accountability Project that advocates for accountability in the electoral process through engagement with stakeholders. The first phase involved debriefing judges, judicial officers, and lawyers handling election cases, with a focus on Electoral Dispute Resolution (EDR) processes. The second phase involves publishing the Fourth Edition of the Elections Compendium, a vital reference guide for practitioners in the bench, bar, academia, media, and civil society. The compendium reflects the evolving electoral landscape in Kenya and the region, highlighting changes in electoral laws through legislative amendments and judicial pronouncements and it also addresses any gaps

The meeting, which was chaired by Tharaka Constituency member of National Assembly, Hon. George Murugara who chairs the Committee, saw the Commission outline key funding priorities areas that are crucial for the sustenance of the it's operations. The IEBC team was led by Deputy Commission Secretary – Operations Ruth Kulundu accompanied by members of senior management. The primary focus of the meeting was for the Commission to emphasize critical areas that require financial facilitation to ensure that the Commission's continue to function effectively. some of the notable areas that the Commission highlighted for funding include settlement of pending bills, election technology, medical insurance among others. DCS Kulundu while presenting the budget estimates to the committee, justified the budget items and underscored the importance of the National Treasury to fund the proposed budget lines to enable the Commission to deliver on its mandate and enhance its operational capacity

English: National Treasury trains Commission staff on new electronic government procurement and inventory management systems29th Jul 2024. The Commission in collaboration with The National Treasury and ELGIA is holding a 3-day training workshop on the new electronic government procurement system (e-GP), Inventory Management System (IMS) and procurement litigation. The e-G is set to be used by all government entities in the country starting 1st July 2024. The aim of the system is to make procurement easier and faster. Opening the workshop, the Commission Secretary/CEO Marjan Hussein Marjan applauded The National Treasury for taking time to train and ensure the Commission staff are familiar with the new procurement system. He also thanked ELGIA for supporting the training

English: IEBC renews collaboration with UCSPAK to strengthen students role in electoral process29th Jul 2024. The Commission today hosted the leadership of the Universities College Students Peace Association of Kenya (UCSPAK), discussed mutual areas for collaboration and resigned the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen their work relationship. Deputy Commission Secretary - Operations Ruth Kulundu emphasized the Commission's positive working relationship with UCSPAK, particularly in mobilizing their members to participate in electoral processes. Allan Chacha, CEO of UCSPAK, acknowledged the Commission as a crucial stakeholder that has supported good governance in University Student Leader elections through mentorship. He noted that as UCSPAK prepares to unveil its strategic plan later this year, the partnership will enhance youth participation in electoral processes since governance is one of its key pillars. Chacha expressed UCSPAK's intent to strengthen their partnership with the Commission. Under the Governance Pillar the Commission will lead in mentorship of student leaders and aspiring leaders, voter registration, voter education, election observation, boundaries delimitation to equip university students with the electoral processes. Ag. DVEP, Amina Soud, HSC observed that the IEBC–USPACK relationship has been successful and the renewing of the MoU will strengthen future collaboration

English: Gender and equality Commission tours IEBC offices to discuss 2022GE recommendations29th Jul 2024. The National Gender and Equality Commission-Kenya today paid a courtesy call to the IEBC and discussed the 2022GE post election monitoring recommendations. The team was received by Ruth Kulundu, IEBC Deputy Commission Secretary (DCS) - Operations, who said that the Commission is committed to delivering free, fair, transparent, credible and inclusive elections, that ensure participation and engagement of Special Interest Groups (SIGs) throughout the electoral cycle. “NGEC monitored participation and engagement of Special Interest Groups (SIGs) during the 2022 General Election. The findings and key recommendations are contained in the report dubbed "Involvement and Participation of Special Interest Groups (SIGS) in the 2022 General Elections in Kenya,” said Mr. Paul Kuria, Ag. Commission Secretary/CEO NGEC. The report has not only assessed election preparedness and involvement of SIGs as candidates, voters, agents and observers of elections; but it has also documented incidences of gender-based violence and response, violence against women, and inequalities and discrimination encountered by SIGs in the election processes. “IEBC is considering recommendations from our stakeholders as outlined in the #2022GE Post Election Evaluation Report and Election Observation Reports, with the goal of improving the electoral processes”, said Kulundu, IEBC DCS - Operations. Mr. Kuria thanked the Commission for heeding the call for a meeting and taking into account NGEC’s recommendations with a goal of mutual collaboration to improve participation of the SIGs in elections

English: IEBC meets donor partners to review work plan, timeline for projects under Basket Fund29th Jul 2024. The Commission led by Deputy Commission Secretary (DCS) Support Service, Obadiah Keitany, who represented the Commission/CEO Marjan H. Marjan, MBS co-chaired the 9th Project Steering Committee meeting alongside implementing partners from UNDP, UNWomen, UN Human Rights - Office in Kenya, European Union, Germany Ambassy, Embassy of Ireland and Italian Embassy in Kenya. The meeting, which was held on on 29th May, 2024, sought to receive an approval of the revised annual work plan, new timelines and review the status report of the projects under the Basket Fund. UNDP Kenya Deputy Resident Representative - Programme Madelena Monoja noted that the project, which started in 2021 to support elections in Kenya, has had numerous achievements, which enabled IEBC to conduct a credible 2022 General Election that was peaceful, inclusive and countered misinformation and propaganda throughout the election cycle The Commission expressed its appreciation for the support received from the Development Partner’s Basket Fund as it was pivotal in ensuring that IEBC discharges its mandate The Commission is currently seeking support to review the strategic plan 2020-2024, which will inform the development of Strategic Plan 2024-2028 & the 2027 Election Operations Plan; rolling out of the paralegal training project; conduct of online voter registration and education and peer learning on electoral legal framework and election technologies. Further this support will be channeled to the establishment of Commission's technology testing, scrutiny and training lab.; establishment of a Customer Experience Centre- preliminary operations and piloting; development of career progression guidelines and acquisition of the fact checking tools to address mis/disinformation such as iVerify, iMonitor+ tool. The Commission is also keen to ensure all supported activities are duly implemented, and results shared as planned

English: Somalia Prime Minister pays courtesy call on Commission, learns Kenyas electoral process29th Jul 2024. The Commission on Wednesday, May 8, 2024 hosted a delegation from the Federal Republic of Somalia led by Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre. The delegation was in the country benchmarking on various areas of interest including election management ahead of its country’s elections set for June 2024. In particular, the Somalia delegation was keen to learn how the Commission conforms to the principles of good governance while undertaking its mandate. The Commission Secretary/CEO Marjan H. Marjan welcomed the delegation and appreciated them for their recognition of the role the Commission plays in promoting democracy in Kenya. Somalia Prime Minister noted that Kenya’s election management body has proved to be instrumental in steering the country through electoral legal reforms and lauded IEBC for its commitment to conduct and supervise elections, carry out verifiable voter registration, undertake voter education and settle electoral disputes, which have set the bar high in Africa and the world. The Commission has shown professionalism and hinged its operations on the Constitution of Kenya. Somalia is keen to learn as it strives to strengthen its democratic processes despite the challenges it faces,” said Somalia PM Hamza Abdi Barre. The delegation was taken through the electoral processes, especially how the Commission has leveraged on electoral technology to carry out biometric voter registration, inspection and verification of register of voters, and results transmission to enhance credibility of Kenya’s elections

English: IEBC joins Kenyans to mark National Tree Growing Day, plants trees in Ngong Road Forest, Bomas Block29th Jul 2024. The Commission led by Commission Secretary/CEO Marjan H. Marjan, MBS on Friday may 10th 2024 joined Kenyans in marking the National Tree Growing Day by planting trees at the Ngong Road Forest, Bomas Block, as part of the efforts to protect the environment and mitigate against the effects of climate change. The choice of this location rings a bell to many Kenyans because Bomas of Kenya, during the electioneering period, is synonymous with the Commission as it serves as the National Tallying Centre. The Commission is proud to join other Kenyans to make a positive contribution to our planet earth and support the national goal of increasing Kenya’s forest cover through planting 15 billion trees by 2032. Importantly, the Commission stands in solidarity with Kenyans who are affected by the floods and condoles with the families that lost their loved ones occasioned by the continuing floods being experienced in the country. Today is not only about tree planting, but also an opportunity to create awareness in our workplaces, families and society on the importance of environmental conservation and why the country needs to meet its target of increasing forest cover. The Commission has undertaken over 25 tree growing exercises across the country and continues to collaborate with relevant institutions to support efforts towards maintaining the planted trees so as to ensure they grow to maturity. These trees, planted with care and foresight, will not only benefit the current generation but will also stand as a legacy for future generations to cherish and protect

English: Commission submits views on proposed IEBC (Amendment) Bill, 2024 to joint JLAC Committee of Senate and National Assembly24th Apr 2024. The Commission appeared before the joint Senate and National Assembly Justice and Legal Affairs Committee (JLAC) led by Chairpersons Hon. George Murugara and Senator Hillary Sigei to submit views on the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (Amendment) Bill, 2024 (National Assembly Bill No. 10 of 2024) at the County Hall, Mini Chambers, Nairobi. The Commission Secretary and CEO, Marjan H. Marjan, MBS led the IEBC team in the presentation of its Memorandum before the committee. Marjan appreciated the progressive nature of the bill in enhancing the efficacy of the Commission and its processes. The Bill intends to review provisions of Sections 2 (Interpretation); 7A (Vacancy in the office of Chairperson and members); 10 (Secretary to the Commission); 36 (Procedure for delimitation of electoral boundaries); First Schedule (Procedure for appointment of Chairperson and Members of the Commission), Second Schedule (Provisions of conduct of the business and affairs of the Commission) and Fifth Schedule (Provisions relating to boundary delimitation) of the IEBC Act considering emerging reforms. The IEBC made submissions which highlighted the relevant legal framework, justification, and proposals for review. In addition, IEBC submitted comments on the implications of the proposed amendments

English: CEO Marjan speaks on opportunities, risks involved with AI use in elections management24th Apr 2024. Information Systems Audit and Control Association (ISACA) Kenya Chapter held its annual conference in Mombasa from 8th to 12th April 2024. The conference, which is themed Digital Trust: Charting the Course for a Resilient Future explored the ground-breaking confluence of digital trust, emerging technology, and the evolution of Artificial Intelligence (AI). Commission Secretary and CEO Marjan H. Marjan, MBS, who is a member of ISACA Kenya Chapter and one of the key speakers in the conference, made a presentation on the opportunities and inherent risks in the use of AI in elections management. “Election Management Bodies (EMBs) stand to benefit from the emergence of AI especially in voter education, elections results management and communication. AI tools can be used to quickly translate electoral and digital documents to difference languages, countercheck and verify election results as well as analyze and identify patterns in provisional voting among others,” said Marjan. The CEO added that the Commission deployed AI in the 2022 General Election by using a WhatsApp Bot to disseminate electoral information, analyzing the Register of Voters (RoV) to check for deduplications and partnered with International Foundation for Election Systems (IFES) to develop a hate speech digital and social media monitoring tool. “AI is being used to develop and spread misinformation, disinformation and mal-information on digital and social media platforms, escalate hate speech, increase the digital divide among other risk factors,” said Marjan

English: IEBC attends electoral management bodies conference, discusses use of AI in 2022 GE2nd Apr 2024. The Commission took part in the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Conference for Electoral Management Bodies (EMBs) in Africa that was organized by Yiaga Africa in Nairobi on 16 March 2024. The Commission Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Marjan Hussein Marjan, MBS, shared insightful perspectives on the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) by EMBs. In his presentation, Mr. Marjan emphasized the practical applications of AI that the Commission employed during the 2022 General Election including voter registration to avoid deduplication of voters, and use of mobile applications aimed at providing electoral related information with the aim of empowering voters to make informed decisions. The CEO underlined the important collaboration the Commission has forged with the International Foundation for Electoral Systems (IFES) that led to creating a social media monitoring tool powered by AI that monitored instances of hate speech. In addition, the Commission partnered with META to address misinformation and disinformation. Marjan's presentation underscored the need for capacity building and accountability of EMBs as they embrace AI in order to enhance efficiency

English: IFES Director for Africa pays courtesy call, pledges continuous support to Commission2nd Apr 2024. International Foundation for Electoral Support (IFES) Regional Director for Africa Clara Cole last week paid a courtesy call to IEBC's Commission Secretary/CEO, Marjan Hussein Marjan, MBS. The two had fruitful discussion including evaluating IFES' support to IEBC over time and agree on potential areas for collaboration to assist the Commission meet its Constitutional mandate. The discussions also covered IEBC's approach to managing misinformation and disinformation, digital media and social media influence on elections management, pre-election activities, status of the electoral boundaries exercise and the National Dialogue Committee report. Additionally, the meeting deliberated on the proposed artificial intelligence guidelines for election management bodies that were unveiled during the Artificial Conference held in Nairobi on 16th and 17th March 2024. The CEO appreciated the immense support that IFES provided in the lead up and during the 2022 General Election and the renewed support that was availed post 2022 GE. Mr Marjan also shared a number of possible areas for partnership and collaboration between IEBC and IFES. Ms. Cole, on her part, acknowledged the Commission's appreciation and assured that IFES will continue to commit to the collaboration and will explore all the opportunities available to ensure the Commission delivers on its mandate. Ms. Cole was accompanied by Mr. Obaje Ukeh, Country Director IFES Kenya, Ms. MacKenzie Hempe, Senior Programs Officer IFES Africa and Ms. Dorothy Atieno, Senior Programs Officer IFES Kenya

English: Faith Mony Odhiambo voted President as Commission conducts election for Law Society of Kenya2nd Apr 2024. The Law Society of Kenya (LSK) called upon the Commission to conduct its elections on February 29 across the country. Albert Gogo, the Nairobi County Elections Manager, was appointed the Returning Officer for the election, which were conducted in all the counties. LSK had declared vacant the position of President, Vice-President, Members of Council, Male Representative to the Judicial Service Commission (JSC) and Members of the Advocates Disciplinary Tribunal (ADT). Faith Mony Odhiambo was voted in as the new Law Society of Kenya president succeeding Eric Theuri, who served as President for a two-year term from March 2022. Odhiambo edged out four other candidates after she registered 3,113 votes ahead of her closest rival Peter Wanyama who secured 2,165 votes. Carolyne Kamende finished third in the tight race with 888 votes. Fourth placed Bernard Ng'etich managed 833 votes, while Njoki Mboce got 511 votes. Odhiambo led in all the 6 polling stations at the Milimani Law Courts, and regions like in Nyeri, Homa bay, Nanyuki, Kisii, Machakos, Kisumu and Nakuru. A total of 7,521 out of the 15,715 registered members cast their vote with only 11 votes being declared invalid

English: IEBC Meets Swedish Ambassador to Discuss Legal Reforms and Election Preparedness21st Nov 2023. The Commission Secretary/CEO, Marjan Hussein Marjan, together with Directors Moses Sunkuli, Lorna Onyango and Chrispine Owiye, held a meeting with the new Swedish Ambassador to Kenya Caroline Vicini at the Swedish Embassy in Nairobi and discussed areas of collaboration, including electoral reforms and election preparedness on 28th September, 2023. Marjan told Vicini that the Commission, among others, has over time facilitated electoral legal reforms, voter registration, voter education and related activities, deployment of technology and boundaries delimitation. “The Commission made deliberate efforts to have in place a robust electoral legal framework for the conduct of elections by generating and reviewing election-related legislations and submitting the same to Parliament for consideration,” said Marjan. The CEO added that in the run up to the 2022 General Election, the Commission held several voter education activities and stakeholder engagements and, specifically, met with Justice and Legal Affairs Committee (JLAC) of the National Assembly to deliberate on electoral issues. However, despite a raft of challenges that affected its operations, the Commission, through the basket fund (UNDP), received funding to support its processes. Marjan recommended for immediate enactment of a robust legal framework to facilitate citizens living outside Kenya to participate in electoral processes

English: Public Service Commission Finance Team Visits IEBC to Benchmark on Accounts System21st Nov 2023. The Parliamentary Service Commission (PSC) finance team visited the Commission on 12 th October 2023 to benchmark on the adoption of IPSAS Accrual Basis of accounting which IEBC adopted in 2011/2012 financial year. PSC is in the process of transiting from IPSAS Cash to IPSAS Accrual in the preparation of its financial statements. Deputy Commission Secretary (DCS - Support Services), CPA Obadiah Keitany, welcomed the PSC team saying that the Commission did not take the visit for granted and noted that IEBC was ready to assist PSC in the transition process. The DCS was accompanied by CPA Patrick Nyakira, CPA Clifford Rono and CPA Muhamed Shee. The IPSAS cash basis recognizes revenues when received and expenses when paid, while accrual basis recognizes revenue when earned and expenses when incurred. The adoption of IPSAS Accrual Basis of accounting offers greater accountability, transparency and openness in reporting use of public resources. “The Commission first adopted the IPSAS Accrual Basis of Accounting in 2012 because it offered greater transparency and accountability in the use of public funds,” observed CPA Patrick Nyakira

English: Commission Exhibition Booth Voted Best Community Service Stand at Eldoret National ASK Show10th Mar 2023. The Commission participated in the Eldoret National Agricultural Society of Kenya Show from 1st to 4th March 2023. The theme was 'Promoting Climate Smart Agriculture & Trade Initiates for Sustainable Economic Growth'. Throughout the five-day exhibition, the Commission staff were at hand to answer questions on the electoral process including the conduct of referendum, Continuous Voter Registration, Voter Education and Boundary Delimitation. Thousands of students and members of the public stopped by the IEBC exhibition stand to learn more about the Commission’s mandate and Kenya’s electoral processes. English: Commission Successfully Conducts Six By-elections on 8th December 202221st Dec 2022. The Commission successfully conducted six by-elections for Bungoma County Senatorial election and County Assembly Wards (CAWs) in Ololmasani (Narok County), Kyome/Thaana Ward (Kitui County), Utawala (Nairobi City County), Mumias North (Kakamega County) and South Gem (Siaya County). English: Mombasa ASK Show: IEBC Voted Best in Promotion of National Cohesion and Integration12th Nov 2022. The Commission interacted with the voters and received feedback at the Mombasa International Show, months after it successfully conducted the 2022 General Election. In doing so, the Commission erected an exhibition stand at the Mkomani Showground, which drew in the public to among other things address any queries on the Commission’s mandate and election processes. The Commission interacted with the voters and received feedback at the Mombasa International Show, months after it successfully conducted the 2022 General Election. Among the dignitaries that visited the Commission’s stand were Deputy President, Rigathi Gachagua, and Mombasa Governor, Abdulswamad Sharrif. “The Commission has done well to open a stand and engage the public on how to conduct elections. It is also important that the Commission teaches high school students election processes,” said Gachagua. During the Show, the Commission’s exhibition stand was nominated as the best in promoting national cohesion and integration development. The Mombasa International Show had taken a two-year break due to Covid-19, and it marked its 119 th edition. The Mombasa International Show, which is managed by the Agriculture Society of Kenya (ASK), ran from 2 to 6 November, 2022

English: IEBC builds youth capacity on electoral process2nd Dec 2021. The Commission held a 5-day workshop for Youth Coordinating Committee (YCC) members to build their capacity on the electoral process and timelines. The workshop, which took place from 29 November to 3 December 2021 in Machakos County, was organized by the Directorate of Voter Education, Partnerships and Communications (DVEP&C) with support from County Election Managers Joseph Merem (Nairobi), Eisha Mohamed (Makueni) and Joyce Wamalwa (Machakos). Dr. Joseph Mele took participants through the Elections Operations Plan (EOP), Eisha Mohamed made a presentation on voter education strategies ahead of ECVR II and 2022 GE, while Joyce Wamalwa had a tutorial on identifying gaps in meaningful engagement of youth in the electoral process. The YCC members are expected to mobilize youth to participate in IEBC’s programmes and activities in the 47 counties and 290 constituencies across the country, and provide support in development and distribution of youth targeted voter Information, Education and Communication (IEC) materials. The workshop brought together 37 participants from different youth-serving and youth-led organizations around the country including Universities and College Students’ Peace Association of Kenya (UCSPAK), Siasa Place, Youth Café, Badili Africa, Youth Agenda, Policy Talks Africa, Election Observation Group (ELOG) and National Youth Council. YCC is a consortium of youth led and serving organizations that promote peace and good governance in the country. It creates and coordinates activities that will offer a conducive environment and opportunities for young people to significantly engage in the electoral processes

English: Annual Voter Education Week (AVEW) 2021 Launched22nd Jun 2021. The Commission launched the Annual Voter Education Week (AVEW) across all the 47 Counties and 290 constituencies countrywide on Monday, 14th June, 2021. The national launch was held at the Bomas of Kenya (BoK) with attendees expressing their satisfaction with the activity. The week-long event commenced on 14th June and will end on 20th June 2021. The event will provide the Commission an opportunity to listen and address concerns from the members of the public on all electoral issues. During his address, The IEBC Chairman Wafula Chebukati asked Kenyans to take advantage of the week to learn more about Commission programmes. The Chair asked all stakeholders to play their part in ensuring free fair and transparent elections. At the County Level, County Elections Managers (CEMs) customized their launches to appeal to the local population and fit the environment in their respective Counties. They undertook various activities including tree planting, town hall meetings, school visits, face to face conversations while undertaking voter registration all these in strict compliance with COVID 19 containment measures set by Ministry of Health. The theme of this year's AVEW is "Inclusive Engagement and Education for a Stronger Democracy." "The Commission has now turned its focus towards the 2022 General Election, the boundaries review and any other electoral activity that may arise during the intervening period." Said Chebukati concluding that the AVEW activities will be undertaken with strict compliance to the Ministry of Health (MoH) and Commission's COVID-19 protocols

English: IEBC Galole Conducts Hola Primary School Students Council Elections17th Feb 2021. The Commission is dedicated to its call to educate school going children on the significance of democracy as part of its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR). IEBC Constituency office in Galole undertook the task of conducting student council elections for Hola primary School.Hola Primary school is a mixed day public school located near Hola town in Chewani Ward, Galole Constituency, Tana River County. IEBC Teamin Galole started off by conducting voter education for the electorate and the to be poll officials who comprised of teachers and the school's administration, in order to equip them with the necessary skills for the conduct the student's elections. The Team also supervised candidates' campaigns to ensure fairly allocation of campaign time as well as use of acceptable campaign strategies by the candidates. The Team graciously provided Logistical support to the school by printing ballot papers and certificates and also providing ballot boxes.The elections had 10 elective positions. These were: President/Deputy president; Speaker/Deputy Speaker; Senator (Pre-Primary, Grade 3 & 4 and Standard 6 to 8); Member of Parliament for each class, CS education; CS ICT & External Relations; CS Environment, Health & Sanitation; CS Welfare & Special Needs; CS Sports & Culture; and CS Justice & Cohesion. The elections were conducted in a smooth manner with no incident. The school's administration was grateful to the Commission for the help accorded to the school in the conduct of the elections and the voter education session conducted to add to their knowledge on elections in Kenya. IEBC was represented by Abdallah Chikophe, CEC Galole who also presented the winners with certificates. "Children are the living messages we send to a time we will not see" - John F. Kennedy

English: IEBC Conducts Unoa Primary School Student Council Elections24th Feb 2020. The Commission supports and conducts student council elections as part of its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiatives to foster a culture of democracy and good governance in schools. It is against this backdrop that IEBC staff from Makueni County presided over Unoa Primary School Student Council Elections on Thursday 6th February, 2020. Unoa Primary School is a Public Primary School, located in Makueni Town, Makueni Constituency, Makueni County. The school has a student population of 1,011. IEBC Makueni County Staff led by the CEM Eisha Mohamed conducted voter education, monitored campaigns and trained election officials who were picked from the student fraternity. The team further provided logistical and technical support to the school and partnered with teachers and the school administration. The election had two elective positions namely: School Captain and Speaker. The voter education conducted on the student was so effective that only 3 rejected votes were reported. The election took place in an orderly manner, losers conceded defeat and the school administration, teachers and students termed the exercise as free, fair and transparent

English: IEBC Participates in the Annual Lamu Cultural Festival16th Dec 2019. IEBC through its Lamu County Office participated in this year's Lamu Cultural Festival. The Festival took place from 12th to 16th December, 2019 in Lamu Island which is a part of the Lamu Archipelago of Kenya. Lamu Cultural Festival is one of the best attended community-based cultural festivals in Kenya which aims at promoting the rich Swahili culture, and open up the archipelago to outsiders. The Festival is a celebration of the past and the future, and the beliefs and traditions that are the heart and soul of the Lamu community. Each year, Lamu Town comes to life during the annual Festival. Several competitions and races are staged. These include traditional Swahili poetry, Henna painting and Bao competition. It is in this backdrop that the IEBC Lamu County office led by the CEM, Mohamed A. Ali sought to participate in the event as it would offer the Commission a great platform for interacting with community leaders, visitors and members of the public and educated them of IEBC's Mandate and of the elections cycle through voter education and dissemination of voter education materials. The IEBC Team from Lamu County erected a Stand at the Festival. At the Stand the Team provided services such as voter information, voter registration, and sensitization of the public on the electoral cycle and sharing of electoral timelines. The activities allowed the team to reach out to a bigger audience educating them while distributing voter education materials like brochures, banners, fliers and posters

English: IEBC Successfully Conducts Kibra Poll11th Nov 2019. The Commission successfully conducted the Kibra MNA by-election on Thursday, November 7, 2019. The by-election was occasioned by death of Hon. Ken Okoth on 26th July, 2019 from complications caused by colorectal cancer. The Commission undertook sufficient training of election officials, early dispatch of election materials and briefing of relevant stakeholder prior to and during the exercise, to ensure the election was free, fair and credible. The campaign period ended on Monday 4th November, 2019 at 6pm being 48 hours to the by-election as required by law. Of the 24 candidates cleared to run in the by-election, Okoth Bernard Otieno of ODM Party emerged victorious with 24,636 votes after beating his closest challenger McDonald Mariga of Jubilee party who garnered 10,280 votes out of the 42,037 valid votes cast. The turnout was 35%. Kibra Constituency has 5 wards, 183 polling stations and 118,856 registered voters. Statutory Forms can be downloaded at https://forms.iebc.or.ke/

English: IEBC Presides over Student Council Elections for St. Theresas Girls28th Oct 2019. On 26th July, 2019 the Commission through the Bobasi constituency supervised student's council election for St. Theresas Nyangusu Girls secondary school. The Secondary School is a girl boarding school located in Ritumbe Ward, in Kisii County. The election was conducted in-line with the IEBC's CSR initiative to foster a culture of democracy and good governance in schools. Preparations for the election commenced with voter education sessions with students, the school administration and teachers. The sessions provided an opportunity to demonstrate the voting procedure, roles of the various election officials and how to mark ballot papers. At the end of the sessions, roles that each party would play in the election were defined: students would play the role of polling and counting clerks, teachers would serve as presiding officers or deputy presiding officers while the role of Returning officer and the deputy returning officer were to be played by constituency CEC and CAA respectively. The elections had for eight elective positions namely; President, Deputy President, Sanitary Secretary, Laboratory Secretary and Class Secretaries for Form 1W, Form 2W and Form 3W. All 351 registered voters (students) cast their votes in the election. The election was peaceful and conducted in a smooth manner that portrayed transparency, resulting in free, fair and credible election. The winners were there after issued with the certificates by the Returning officer

English: Stakeholder Engagements ahead of Kibra by-election28th Oct 2019. The Commission is committed to ensuring the 7th November, 2019 MNA by-elections in Kibra are conducted in a transparent, credible and violence-free manner as this will reinforce IEBC's commitment to Moving Kenya Towards a Stronger Democracy. With less than two weeks to the by-election the Commission has intensified stakeholder engagements and voter education with a goal of encouraging peaceful elections, increasing voter's participation in the by-election, and reducing spoiled and rejected votes. It is against this backdrop that the Commission met with Political Parties, Candidates, Security Agents and Government Officials on 22nd October, 2019 to brief them on the level of preparedness for the Kibra MNA by-election. The meeting also gave the Commission an opportunity to encourage the stakeholders to adhere to the Electoral Code of Conduct in order to create a climate of tolerance, free political campaigning, and open public debate that will go along way in promoting conditions that are conducive to free and fair elections. The Commission also met with special interest groups: Women, Youth and Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) on 23rd October, 2019 to equip them with information about the electoral process with a view to increasing their participation in the upcoming by-elections. The groups are also community ambassadors in the Constituency who will work alongside ward based voter educators to educate voters on the voting procedure, how to mark a ballot paper, votes tallying, and results transmission among many others. The Commission plans to meet with Election Observers and the Media on 30th October, 2019

English: IEBC presides over Silibwet High School Elections28th Oct 2019. IEBC through its Kuresoi South Constituency office offered support in the administration of student council elections at Silibwet High School on 20th June 2019. The Kuresoi South Constituency is one of the eleven constituencies within Nakuru County. It is the furthest constituency West of the County, with a voting population of 55,661 people (2017 GE Data) and four county assembly wards namely Keringet, Tinet, Kiptahich and Amalo. Silibwet High School is a public school located within Keringet Ward with a student population of 210. The elections had six elective positions namely: Chairperson, Games Secretary, Environment Secretary, Dining Hall Secretary and Class Secretary for Forms 1 and 2 classes. A number of positions were unopposed (only one candidate contestants) consequently as per the school's election laws the unopposed candidates were issued with certificates. The position of Dining Hall Secretary was the most contested position and attracted six (6) candidates. Noticeably, there was a tie between the two candidates contesting for the position; John Kigen and Philemon Ngeno. As per the rules of elections there was a re-run. In the re-run Philemon Ngeno carried the day. The school administration with help from IEBC customized the ballot papers, polling station results forms and other administrative forms for the purpose of the elections. The team from IEBC took the opportunity to carry out voter education on students and the schools administration regarding election operations and processes in Kenya. Students and teachers were briefed on the eve of elections on what was expected of them using an interactive Q&A session that led to tremendous interaction with students on matters of election in Kenya

English: Voters engage with IEBC at the Nairobi International Trade Fair (NITF)8th Oct 2019. As has become a tradition, once again IEBC took its outreach strategies to the Mwananchi by setting up a one-stop-shop stand that showcased electoral processes and information. The Commission participated in this year's Nairobi International Trade Fair (NITF) at Jamhuri Showground in Kibra Constituency that opened its door to the public on Monday September 30th and closed on Saturday October 5th, 2019. NITF is the largest Trade Fair in the East African Region and brings together regional and global exhibitors to display and demonstrate their services and products to an ever growing audience. This year, over 500 exhibitors participated in the Show which is ran under the theme "Promoting Innovation and Technology in Agriculture and Trade". The Trade fair was held in Kibra Constituency which coincidentally will be having a by-election on November 7th, 2019 to elect their Member of National Assembly. Members of the public from the Constituency who visited the stand were mostly interested in checking their registration details and seeking to understand the Voter registration procedure. Boundary Delimitation was another area of great interest from members of the public. They were interested in knowing whether, when and which criteria will be employed by the Commission in conducting the delimitation process. School children showed great interest in the Stand, they spent time reading the contents of detailed textual and pictorial Storyboards especially the board on CSR that portrays our efforts and commitment in conducting student elections. They were also interested in the mock polling station where they were issued with sample ballot papers and got to 'vote'

English: SOKU gets support from the Commission8th Oct 2019. Kibabii University conducted their 2nd ever Students Council of the University elections on 26th April, 2019 with support and guidance of IEBC. Kibabii University is a public university located in Bungoma. The University was previously a constituent college of Masinde Muliro University of Science and Technology (MUST) but was granted its Charter in November, 2015. The Commission through the Bungoma County office was invited by the University as independent observers to oversee the election and give recommendations on areas of improvements. The University employs the Electoral College system where students (voters) cast ballots for delegates also known as "electors". The delegates afterwards vote for the student leadership. A total of 18 students (delegates) were elected to the Electoral College by the student voters. i.e. University students who qualified to vote. Those delegates then voted in the seven (7) members of the executive, namely Chairperson, Vice Chairperson, Secretary General, Treasurer, Special Interests Secretary, Academic Secretary, Accommodation Secretary and Security Secretary. The election was conducted in a smooth and peaceful manner although it was marked by low turnout which will require improved voter education in the subsequent elections to ensure high voter turnout. The school administration urged the students to participate in large numbers in future elections to exercise their electoral rights and promote democracy in their school

English: IEBC and Kenyatta University Partner for Civic Education17th Sep 2019. Kenyatta University (KU) through its Directorate of Capacity Development and consultancy services (KU-CDCS) paid the Commission a courtesy call to share a partnership proposal, which intends to address informational gaps especially in the area of referendum. The University proposed a collaborative undertaking with IEBC to build the technical skills stakeholders on the referendum process and its projected outcomes. The university felt the need to build the technical capacity of stakeholders so that they can sufficiently engage in matters referendum. The University further requested the drafting and signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with IEBC. Other Proposed areas of collaboration include capacity building for security organs and boundaries delimitation processes, training of electoral staff and stakeholders, building skills on knowledge management, collaborative development and management of an e-learning electoral platform. The Commission has continuously partnered with like-minded organizations to enhance civic and democratic tenets in Kenya. A partnership with institutions of higher learning would enable the Commission to reach out to the untapped population of youth in those institutions through civil education. It was observed that the Commission, being a neutral arbiter in the referendum chain, shall not focus on a particular initiative but shall confine itself on the processes of conducting a referendum during trainings. Both institutions agreed on drafting and signing an MOU on other areas of collaboration including capacity building for security organs and boundaries delimitation processes, training of electoral staff and stakeholders, building skills on knowledge management and a collaborative development, management of an e-learning electoral platform. The meeting was held on Monday 9th September, 2019 at the IEBC headquarters and attended by line Directors and Managers led by Obadiah Keitany who was the session chair sitting in for Ag. CS/CEO Marjan H. Marjan

English: IEBC Gender and Social Inclusion Policy Internal Validation Workshop17th Sep 2019. In 2016, the Commission, in Partnerships with United Nations Development Programmme (UNDP) commenced the process of developing a Gender and Social Inclusion Policy (GSIP) to mainstream special interest groups in all electoral processes. A series of inclusive and participatory workshops with key stakeholder groups, Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) and Key Informant Interviews (KIIs) coupled with review of primary and secondary data of various policies documents, reports and international human rights instruments informing political participation aided in the preparation of the inception report and literature review document. Report of the challenges facing Special Interest Groups formed the basis for formulating the broad policy areas and the policy statements. The draft policy was presented to the IEBC Commissioners and CEMS for scrutiny and input and later to the Technical Working Group (TWG) who provided vital feedback and further input. Their input has been incorporated in the document and it's now ready for validation by both internal and external stakeholders. It is against this backdrop that the Commission through Directorate of Voter Education Partnerships &Communications held a one-day workshop in Nairobi with Directors and Manager to subject the draft policy to internal validation. The workshop provided the secretariat with an opportunity to scrutinize the document for accuracy and validity. A similar workshop with external stakeholders will be held at a later date. Commissioner Prof. Abdi Guliye attended the validation workshop, alongside Directors, Managers and Nairobi County IEBC Staff, who gave their inputs and recommendations that will be incorporated in the draft policy

English: IEBC Dispute Resolution Committee17th Sep 2019. IEBC's Dispute Resolution Committee (DRC) heard a complaint filed by the Jubilee Party of Kenya nominee, Mcdonald Mariga Wanyama seeking to appeal the decision of the Kibra Returning Officer in the forthcoming MNA by-election. The Returning Officer on Tuesday 10th September, 2019 disqualified Mariga from vying in the by-election as his registration details could not be found in the voters roll. The DRC is chaired by IEBC Chairman Wafula Chebukati with Commissioners Boya Molu and Prof. Abdi Guliye as members. The Committee heard the Complainant’s, Respondent’s and Interested Parties’ submissions on the matter and will give its determination on Monday 16th September, 2019 at 10.00 a.m

English: IEBC Participates in Mombasa International Show11th Sep 2019. Close to 200 local and international exhibitors are showcasing various goods and services at the ongoing Mombasa International Show (MIS). The five-day Show which runs from 4th to 8th September, 2019 is being held at the Mkomani showground, Nyali constituency in Mombasa County. This year's theme is 'Promoting Innovation and Technology in Agriculture and Trade'. His Excellency the President of the Republic of Kenya, Uhuru Kenyatta officially opened the International Show on Thursday 5th September, 2019 and urged the exhibitors to invest in innovative and cost effective programs that will ensure steady growth of the economy as well as create jobs for the Kenyan youth. The Mombasa International Show is the 3rd ASK event that the Commission has participated in this year following successful participation in Nakuru and Kisumu Shows in the Month of July, 2019. The Commission will further participate in the upcoming Nairobi International Trade Fair (NITF) starting Monday, 30th September to Sunday, 6th October 2019 at Jamhuri Park Showground located in Kibra Constituency. IEBC hopes to engage voters in the constituency ahead of the by-election scheduled to take place on 7th November, 2019

English: IEBC Visits Sahajanand Special School19th Aug 2019. IEBC Kilifi South Constituency Office, led by the RO Aisha Abubakar, paid a visit to Sahajanand Special School on 29th January, 2019. The school is home to over 1000 students from around the East African Community with various forms of mental and physical disabilities. The mission of the school is to restore hope, self-esteem and confidence of children with special needs through the provision of a homely environment where they are treated with love and care, whilst also being educated to empower them with skills and knowledge that would promote independence and sustainability. The school visit was undertaken in an effort to reach existing and potential voters in the constituency as part of its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR). The team from IEBC presented the school with a small token for the students. The team also held voter education sessions with the school's administration and students

English: IEBC Conducts Camp Brethren Christian School Elections19th Aug 2019. The IEBC Gilgil Constituency office presided over Camp Brethren Christian student council elections on 1st March, 2019. The School is located approximately 32 KMs from the constituency office in Eburu/ Mbaruk Ward, Gilgil Constituency, Nakuru County. The school invited the Commission to preside over their elections in a bid to enhance leadership in the school by embracing democratic elections. All students participated in the elections and had a chance to vote for their leaders in various positions that included School President and Deputy President, Governors for each class, Senators (Representatives of various school departments) and MCAs (Class representatives). The elections were officiated by Mr. Nguthu, the Gilgil CEC, who played the role of Returning Officer. He was deputized by Mr. Kamau, the Gilgil CAA, while teachers played the role of presiding officers and clerks. Prior to the day of elections, Mr. Nguthu and Mr. Kamau conducted voter education, oversaw candidate nominations, monitored campaigns and also conducted voter registration. They also provided logistical and technical support to the school while being assisted by teachers and the school administration. The elections took place in an orderly manner, demonstrating that the electoral process can truly be free, fair and transparent

English: IEBC Sponsors the Nairobi Royal Ladies Open 2019 Tournament12th Jul 2019. The third pillar of the IEBC Strategic Plan 2015-2020 seeks to enhance public trust and participation in the electoral process. This is reiterated by the Commission's Gender and Social Inclusion Policy that is aimed at improving the political participation of women and other Article 100 groups. Further, the Commission aims to build bridges and networks with the community and other stakeholders as per the CSR policy. It is against this backdrop that the Commission heeded to the request by the Royal Nairobi Golf Club to sponsor the Royal Ladies Open Tournament 2019. The Royal Ladies Open Tournament is an annual event that brings together female golfers from around the country to play golf as a way of women empowerment. This year (2019) brought together 130 female golfers, 210 caddies and over 20 guests to the tournament. The tournament took place on 6th July, 2019. The Commission, through the Nairobi County Office and the Directorate of Voter Education, Partnerships and Communications (DVEP&C), conducted voter education to the attendees; educating them on the mandate of the Commission, its programs and activities. The team also provided a KIEMS kit for those in attendance to check their registration details. The event was attended by Commissioner Prof. Abdi Guliye, Commissioner Molu Boya, Ag. CS/CEO, Marjan H. Marjan, Director VEP&C Immaculate Kassait, MBS, Manager CCA,Tabitha Mutemi and other members of the secretariat drawn from the headquarters and Nairobi IEBC County Office

English: IEBC Presides over Oaklands Junior School Elections28th Jun 2019. On January 25th, 2019 IEBC through its Subukia Constituency Office conducted Oakland's Junior School Elections. The elections provided the Commission an opportunity to expose the students to the electoral process and educate them on the importance of democracy, good governance and the role the Commission plays in Kenyan elections. Preparations for the elections commenced with a sit-down with all stakeholders invested in the elections: School Administration, Teachers, Candidates and Students (voters). The sit-down provided a great opportunity for IEBC officials to conduct voter education sessions with students, teachers and the school administration. The stakeholders were taught how to mark ballot papers, how to cast ballot paper, the role of poll officials during elections and the need for democracy and good governance in the Country. Candidates were also briefed on what is expected of them before and during the elections. On the day of elections, IEBC officials brought election materials to the school, setup class rooms as polling stations and a tallying center. The school had nine elective positions: -President -Minister for Academics -Ministers for Dormitories -Minister for Entertainment -Minister for Interior Security and Coordination -Minister for Sports -Minister for Environment -Minister for Dining -Minister for Health The total number of voters in the elections was 84; teachers played the role of presiding officers while IEBC officials played the role of observers and returning officer. At the end of the voting exercise, the votes were tallied, results forms filled and results formally announced and displayed. Certificates were then issued to those who won the elections. The elections carried on peacefully with no hindrances, two candidates however, disputed the results after counting, the dispute was later overruled as the two candidates had already been disqualified during the nomination process

English: Annual Voter Education Week (AVEW) Launched18th Jun 2019. The Commission launched the Annual Voter Education Week (AVEW) across all the 47 Counties and 290 constituencies countrywide on Monday, 10th June, 2019. The week-long event commenced on 10th June and will end on 16th June 2019. The event will provide the Commission an opportunity to listen and address concerns from the members of the public on all electoral gadgets, tools, policies, activities, processes and procedures. The National Launch of AVEW commenced with a walk dubbed: "Walk for Peaceful Election". IEBC staff and stakeholders participated and distributed voter education materials along the route to Uhuru Park Grounds. The walk was flagged off by IEBC Chairman Wafula Chebukati, Commissioners Prof. Abdi Guliye and Boya Molu and Ag.CS/CEO Marjan H. Marjan at Anniversary Towers. The Walk terminated at Uhuru Park Grounds where the IEBC Chairman delivered his key note address and officially launch AVEW. During his address, The IEBC Chairman urged the entire nation to fully participate in all the planned AVEW activities, encouraging them to, "Karibu tujadiliane" with IEBC Staff across the 47 Counties and 290 constituencies. ( Download Chairman's Speech) At the County Level, County Elections Managers (CEMs) customized their launches to appeal to the local people and fit the environment in their respective Counties. They undertook various activities including tree planting, Barazas, community gatherings, town hall meetings, school visits, face to face conversations while undertaking voter registration among others

English: IEBC Presides over Tabasamu SACCO Elections24th May 2019. On 30th March, 2019 IEBC conducted election for Tabasamu Savings and Credit Co-operative (SACCO). Tabasamu Sacco Society Limited was registered on 18th February, 1977 under Co-operatives Societies Act (Cap 490) of the laws of Kenya as a savings and credit co-operative society. Members of the Society are drawn from teachers, government ministries, parastatals, non-governmental organizations and the private sector. Currently the Society has nearly 4,000 active members and almost all members have accounts in the FOSA. The SACCO wrote to the Kwale IEBC County Office seeking assistance with preparations for their election, citing the need for free, fair and credible election. A team comprising of the Returning Officers for Matuga, Kassim Kaema, and Msambweni, Yusuf Mohamed, embarked on presiding over the elections by providing strategic and non-strategic materials, conducting voter education, monitoring campaigns and training election officials. The election had two elective positions namely: Tsimba Tiwi Board Member and Kinango/Samburu Supersoul Member. The Tsimba Tiwi Board Member election resulted in a tie and a re-run was recommended; and will take place at a later date. Over 100 votes were recorded for this position. Only one candidate was successfully vetted for the position of Kinango/Samburu Supersoul Member as per the Cooperative Society regulations. The Candidate was therefore un-opposed to the ballot; and was hence declared the duly elected member. Such exercises are important to the Commission as they foster ideal democratic principles and good working relationships with stakeholders in the society while enhancing public trust and confidence in the Commission

English: IEBC Presides over KTTI Student Council Elections10th May 2019. On 15th February, 2019 IEBC in conjunction with Kisiwa Technical Training Institute Electoral Commission Board (KTTIECB) held the KTTI Institute's student council elections. The Electoral Board Commission consists of 8 members namely: 5 student commissioners, the Dean of Students, Deputy Chairman and Chairman of the Commission. Elections in KTTI are held each year to choose students leaders in 8 elective positions as mandated in the Institute's Constitution. The positions are: Chairman, Vice chairman, Secretary General, CS Finance, Health Representative, Welfare, Entertainment and Games / Sports Representative. The elections were presided over by CEC Kabuchai - Benson Esuza, who was tasked with coordinating and overseeing all activities during the elections while being assisted by Simon Makokha - DRO Kabuchai Constituency. KTTI Electoral Commission Board deployed sixteen (16) clerks, four (4) security officers and other subordinate staff to help with facilitation and coordination of the election. The Commission provided strategic and non-strategic materials, conducted voter education, monitored campaigns, trained election officials, accredited candidates' agents and finally set up two polling stations for use in the elections. The results were as follows: Emmanuel Samtuk - Chairperson - 732 votes out of 1,141 Maureen Simwa - Vice Chairperson - 673 votes out of 1,163 Teddy Otieno - Sectary General - 532 votes out of 1,144 Daniel Macharia - CS Finance - 756 votes out of 1,146 Justin Sindani - Health Representative - 662 votes out of 1,142 Edith Bulimo - Welfare - 533 votes out of 848 Daniel Were - Entertainment Rep. - 724 votes out of 1,147 Isaac Nzoka - Games and sport Rep. - 590 votes out of 1,148

English: IEBC conducts External Elections in Turkana3rd May 2019. The Commission as stipulated under article 88 of the constitution is mandated to conduct or supervise referenda and elections of any elective body or office. It is for this purpose that the Commission commits to undertake elections for organizations and schools as a way of inculcating democratic tenets in potential and existing voters as part of its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR). On 2nd February 2019, the IEBC Turkana County office presided over Turkana County Drivers and Transport Association (TUCODTA) election,as requested by the Association's sub-committee. The Commission provided electoral materials, conducted voter education, monitored campaigns, trained officials, supported designing & printing of the ballot papers and supervised the voting process. The election had four elective positions as provided for in their governing constitution. The positions are: Chairperson, Deputy Chairperson, General Secretary and Treasurer. The commission used the opportunity to urge eligible voters especially the youth to register in large numbers in the ongoing Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) happening across the country except electoral areas with pending by-elections. He further encouraged media houses present (KBC TV, Radio Maisha, Radio Akicha and a host of local FM stations) to sensitize the public on Voter Registration and other electoral activities. The Commission will continue partnering with willing organizations and schools to conduct elections as such initiatives will ensure exposure to electoral information

English: IEBC Conducts Wajir West Member Of National Assembly By-election29th Apr 2019. The Commission conducted Wajir West Constituency by-election on 25th April, 2019. The by-election was occasioned by a successful election petition in the constituency that saw the incumbent MP Ahmed Kolosh lose his seat following a decision by the Supreme Court on 18th January, 2019 that nullified his win citing irregularities at Qara polling station. The court noted that the number of votes cast at that polling station exceeded that of registered voters. The constituency is one of six constituencies in Wajir County, it has five County Assembly Wards and covers an area of approximately 9,764.3 square kilometers with 27,544 registered voters and 75 polling stations. The Commission adequately prepared for the by-election by ensuring proper training of election officials, early dispatch of election materials and briefing of relevant stakeholder prior to and during the exercise, to ensure the election were free, fair and credible. The Commission cleared five Candidates to contest in the by-election, Mohamed Ahmed Kolosh of Jubilee party emerged victorious with 11,053 votes against his closest challenger Ibrahim Mohamud Abdirahaman who garnered 6,532 votes.The valid votes cast were 17,608 with a turnout of 63.927%. Statutory Forms for the by-election can be downloaded at https://forms.iebc.or.ke/

English: IEBC Successfully Conducts Three By-elections15th Apr 2019. The Commission successfully conducted three by-elections in Lelan CAW, Embakasi South and Ugenya MNA on Friday, April 5th, 2019. The by-elections were occasioned by successful petitions in Embakasi South and Ugenya Constituency and the death of Hon. Tanui Vincent, the elected MCA for Lelan Ward. The Commission adequately prepared for the by-elections by ensuring proper training of election officials, early dispatch of election materials and briefing of relevant stakeholder prior to and during the exercise, to ensure the election were free, fair and credible. The campaign period ended on Tuesday, April 2 nd , 2019 being 48 hours to the by election as required by law. Of the 15 candidates cleared to run in the Embakasi South Constituency, Julius Mawathe of Wiper Democratic Party garnered 21, 628 votes out of the 30,750 votes cast, to win the Embakasi South MNA seat. The turnout was 20.46%. Embakasi South Constituency has 5 wards, 221 polling stations and 150,314 registered voters. Ochieng David Ouma of MDG party emerged victorious with 18,730 votes to win the Ugenya MNA seat. A total of 33,936 votes were cast, which is 57.99% 57,603 registered voters. Of these votes, 33,402 valid while 534 were rejected. of the valid votes cast. Ugenya Constituency has 4 wards, 112 polling stations. Jubilee Party’s Kurgat Priscila Jepkoech clinched the Lelan County Assembly Ward by-election with a total of 3,170 of the 5,185 votes cast. The CAW recorded a voter turnout of 61.98%. Lelan Ward is located in Marakwet West Constituency, Elgeyo Marakwet County and has a total of 8,366 registered voters distributed across 29 polling stations. The Lelan CAW, Embakasi South and Ugenya MNA by-elections Statutory Forms can be downloaded at https://forms.iebc.or.ke/

English: IEBC Meets JLAC to Deliberate on Electoral Legal Reviews25th Mar 2019. Mombasa, 17th March, 2019 The Commission met with members of the Justice and Legal Committee (JLAC) to deliberate on issues of referendum law, election finance campaign laws and boundaries delimitation. The workshop which took place from 17 th to 19 th March, 2019 was supported by Electoral Law and Governance Institute for Africa (ELGIA). On February 12th, 2019 IEBC launched the 2017 Post Election Evaluation Report which highlighted some of the legal challenges experienced by the Commission in the run up to the 2017 General Election and the Fresh Presidential Election. It is in this backdrop that the Commission has resorted to start the process of reviewing governing laws and regulation in an effort to better management of future elections. IEBC Chairman Wafula Chebukati in his remarks during the workshop pledged to work closely with legislators and other election stakeholders to ensure the Country has the relevant electoral laws in place to deliver on transparency and credibility of the electoral processes. Hon. William Cheptumo, the Chairperson of JLAC lauded the Commission's effort to start reviewing the electoral laws in time to avoid last minute amendments that cause confusion and have negative impact on the electoral processes. The meeting was attended by JLAC Chairman and members, IEBC Chairman, Commissioners Prof. Adbi Guliye and Boya Molu, Ag. CS/ CEO Marjan H. Marjan and several members of the secretariat from the Commission and the National assembly

English: Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) Launched17th Oct 2018. CVR targets to grow the 19.3M register of voters by 3% in a year Wote, Makueni, 15th October, 2018 The IEBC has launched a Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) countrywide. The CVR exercise targets to increase the number of voters by at least 3%, from the 19.6 Million voters enrolled as at 2017 to 20.1 Million by June, 2019. The launch was made at Wote town, Makueni County. Prof Kivuta Kibwana said “it is important to conduct civic education on voter registration so as to empower the voters and also to educate them against ethnic mindset when voting” Prof Kibwana thanked IEBC for choosing to launch the important exercise in Makueni. He promised to work closely with IEBC to enhance civic education and voter registration. IEBC’s Chairman, Mr. Wafula Chebukati, said the Commission had addressed issues raised in the KPMG report on the Register of Voters. “We also expect an improvement in the accuracy of the register of voters by implementing the KPMG recommendations”. The Continuous Voter Registration CVR provides an opportunity to: Register eligible voters especially the youth and special interest groups Allow transfers from one electoral area to preferred electoral areas Correct any errors identified by KPMG audit The event was graced by local leaders, among them the Makueni Senator, Mutula Kilonzi Jnr

English: Migori and Central Sakwa By-elections Concluded10th Oct 2018. Voter turnout in Migori was 38.2 and Central Sakwa 42.19 Migori, 9 th October, 2018 Two By-elections, the Migori County Senate and Central Sakwa County Assembly Ward (CAW) in Bondo Constituency (Siaya County) were successfully conducted on Monday, 8 th October, 2018. The Migori seat was won by Mr. George Ochilo Ayacko while the Central Sakwa CAW seat was won by Mr. Carlton Odhiambo Andiego. Voter turnout in both by-elections was low, with 38.2 reported in Migori and 42.19 in Central Sakwa. The Commission did not transmit the results electronically, in real time, since this is not a requirement for non-presidential elections. For the Migori Senatorial by-election, results from polling stations in form 38A were delivered to the Constituency Tallying Centres and after verification the Returning Officers filled form 38B. The Returning Officers deliver the form 38B to the County Returning Officer, who prepared the final results in form 38C. Agents witnessed the filling of both form 38 A and B. They also signed and were given copies. Constituency Returning Officers scan the 38A and upload into a public web portal for public viewing at: forms.iebc.or.ke/form36asakwa and https://forms.iebc.or.ke/migori

English: Training Timelines for Migori, Sakwa By-elections Out6th Sep 2018. Update on Migori Senate and Central Sakwa CAW by-elections Nairobi, 6th September, 2018 Training of poll officials for the October 8 th Migori County Senate and Central Sakwa (Siaya County) by-elections will be conducted as follows: Top level officials- the Trainers of Trainers (TOTs), Returning Officers (ROs) and Deputy Returning Officers (DROs)- 17 th - 28 th , September, 2018. Presiding Officers (POs), Deputy Presiding Officers (DPOs) and Clerks- 1 st -6th October, 2018 The electoral body will recruit the temporary poll officials from the list of officials who have previously been employed to conduct elections. The Commission is also engaging with security agencies to ensure that the by-elections are not only free and fair but also peaceful. The IEBC’s Returning Officials will make arrangements with education officials to ensure minimum disruptions to learning where schools are used as polling stations. Migori Senate and Central Sakwa CAW seat fell vacant following the death of Ben Oluoch Okelo and Joanes Andiego respectively. The candidates who were cleared to vie after presenting their nomination papers to IEBC’s Returning Officers on 9 th and 10 th August, 2018 are: Migori Senate (388,633 registered voters, 826 polling stations) Ochilo Ayacko (ODM), Ogola Dickson (Independent) Jobando Peter Osieko (Green Congress Party) Oketch Eddy Gichuru (Federal Party of Kenya) Otieno Samuel Otieno (Independent) Rugaria Solomon Hodo (Peoples Democratic Party) Central Sakwa County Assembly Ward (11, 827 registered voters, 23 polling stations) Charlton Andiego Odhiambo (ODM) Namal Kenrick Orony (CCP) Meanwhile short term observers can apply for accreditation by downloading forms from the Commission’s website or by applying online at https://accreditation.iebc.or.ke/oms/

English: We are Committed to Credible and Acceptable Polls- Chebukati1st Sep 2018. Commission Chair Mr. Chebukati assures religious group that electoral body will manage elections to the satisfaction of all Nairobi, 23 rd August, 2018 The Unfungamano Joint Forum of Religious Organizations (U-JFRO) has called for measure to ensure that elections are peaceful and not disruptive. Speaking during a consultative meeting with IEBC, Bishop Boniface Adoyo, a trustee of U-JFRO, said “the country goes through difficult times during and after elections. Things need to change, even if it requires a referendum” The team of religious leaders, which comprised trustees and council members, discussed a number of proposals for change on elections and governance with IEBC Commissioners and senior members of the secretariat. IEBC’s Chairman, Mr. Chebukati, said the electoral body is committed to demonstrate independence and accountability in the way it carries out its duties despite the threats to disrupt the independence of the institution. He vowed to carry out elections “to the satisfaction of even the losers”. Mr. Chebukati urged religious organizations to support IEBC in its voter education initiatives. The views given by U-JFRO will be incorporated in the Post Election Exercise process due to be concluded by the end of September, 2018. Led by their Co-Chair Rasmin Chitnis, the U-JFRO team asked IEBC to exercise their independence to support positive change
